issue.title: Umbrella: oracle-anchored binary market-maker — prove-first, venue/instrument-agnostic
issue.body:
> **Tracker — ROBUSTNESS-FIRST.** Edge existence is assumed (a mature, competitive maker market); the gate is implementation robustness, validated by a pre-live backtest of the *built* maker before any live capital.
> Authoritative design lives in the spec-kit feature, not this issue:
> **`specs/488-binary-oracle-maker/spec.md`** (WHAT) + **`specs/488-binary-oracle-maker/plan.md`** (HOW), on branch `docs/488-mm-multi-venue-survey` (basis branch; not merged to main by decision).
> This issue is a thin tracker: summary, status, links, relations. It does **not** restate the plan (single source of truth = the spec) or any versioned fact (e.g. the NT rev — that lives in `Cargo.toml`).

## Summary

A two-sided resting market-maker for Polymarket binary (YES/NO) markets, anchored to bolt's existing oracle fair value, then fanned out to perps/CEX behind a shared agnostic framework. Direction: **robustness-first** (edge existence assumed; the gate is implementation robustness — adverse selection is the dominant cost — with a pre-live backtest of the built maker as the go-live gate); **GM/CG adverse-selection spread** as the primary edge (not Avellaneda-Stoikov/GLFT, which are a units error for a bounded (0,1) binary); **agnostic in three layers** (NT execution adapters / venue capability contract / per-instrument `MarketFamily` seam), implementing the Polymarket-binary path first.

This direction **supersedes** both the original proposal ("port the market-maker-rs apparatus; grid→GLFT; anchor an A-S reservation price") and the interim prove-first framing (an upfront offline edge-proof). Overturned by an actual-code audit + an internal 5-lens adversarial review + a Codex adversarial review, then refocused: makers exist, so edge existence is not in question — robustness is. See the spec for the workstreams (W1 → W8), the pre-live backtest gate, the verified venue/runtime constraints, and acceptance criteria.

## Status

- Design captured in the spec/plan (above). Robustness-first build sequence: **W1+W2 → W3 → W4 → pre-live backtest gate → W5/6 → W7/8**. Per-workstream status of record lives in the spec, not here.
- Build well past "starting" (audit refresh 2026-06-19). Merged to main:
  - W1 venue capability contract — PR #573.
  - Maker monolith decomposition onto shared bolt_v3 helpers (#580): quote_lifecycle PR #584, maker_model + TWO_F64 PR #585, maker_microprice PR #587, pure helper drain PR #602, reservation helper PR #605.
  - Generic maker foundation (primitives + go-live gate scaffolding) — PR #716; maker μ newtype gate + modify dispatch fail-closed seams — PR #820; per-market binding subsystem (PR-A) — PR #822.
- Open / remaining go-live blockers:
  - **Pre-live backtest PASS artifact of the built maker — #812 (the go-live gate; open).**
  - Admission-gate the maker's in-place order modify — #835 (deferred from #820).
  - Maker `[[parameters.markets]]` validation message fix — #844.
  - W6–W8 per the spec sequence.

## Links

- Spec / Plan: `specs/488-binary-oracle-maker/{spec.md,plan.md}`
- Actual-code audit (supersedes the survey's port verdicts): `docs/research/mm-code-audit-2026-05-30.md`
- Market-data provider survey: `docs/research/mm-data-providers-2026-05-31.md`
- Reward research: `docs/bolt-v3/research/polymarket-rewards-2026-05-13.md`

## Relations

- #451 (order admission/submission wrapper — NOT the fair-value hoist)
- #41 (multi-market substrate), #409 (PortfolioSnapshot equity stream), #446/#447 (fee/reward-data provider decoupling)
- #135 / #133 (sibling strategy lines)
- #497 (NT rev SHA doc-drift cleanup — the single-source-of-truth fix this spec models)
- Precursors (execution plumbing only; stop at NT OrderFactory construction): #022-nt-maker-order-scope, #023-nt-order-intent-layer, #023-nt-research-analytics-platform/1-backtesting-engine

issue.title: Unblock bolt-v3 real no-order live connectivity test
issue.body:
Blocks #360.

A real no-order connectivity run was executed at prep head `48201c328468f426d02e81ce06b59a12b1ff9af6` using the local live operator TOML and real AWS SSM/venue connectivity. No order submit, cancel, transfer, tiny-capital command, or live trade was attempted.

Observed result:
- AWS SSM secret resolution passed.
- NT LiveNode build passed.
- Controlled connect was entered.
- Polymarket market data connected and loaded instruments.
- Controlled disconnect completed.
- Redacted report was written to `/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/var/bolt-v3-live/reports/no-submit-readiness.json`.
- Gate acceptance failed because `reference_readiness` failed: `BTCUSDT.BINANCE` was not present in the NT cache.

Concrete blockers:
1. Binance reference data client cannot connect with the pinned NautilusTrader revision. The pinned NT rev is `38b912a8b0fe14e4046773973ff46a3b798b1e3e`; its Binance Spot HTTP client sends `X-MBX-SBE: 3:3` and decodes schema version 3, while Binance now returns schema version 4.
2. Upstream NautilusTrader `develop` at `7c2aafb30fb143069c915a3f2057bb12174405f6` contains Binance SBE schema `3:4` / generated schema version `4`, but a direct dependency bump is not drop-in for Bolt. The experimental compile hit API breaks around `CacheView`, `LiveDataEngineConfig`, Binance environment naming, runtime-capture handler types, and `submit_order` args.
3. Polymarket execution connect appears blocked by the no-order readiness path using NT `LiveNode::start()`. NT `start()` flushes pending data events but does not drive execution-event channels while execution clients connect. Polymarket emits account state during connect, then waits for `POLYMARKET-001` to appear in the NT cache; the account event can sit unprocessed until the adapter times out. NT `LiveNode::run()` has event buffering during execution-client connect, but entering `run()` is not an acceptable shortcut for the no-order readiness gate because it enters the live runner/trader loop.

Acceptance criteria:
- The real no-order connectivity test can pass without submitting/canceling/replacing any order and without entering the live trader loop.
- The redacted report has all required stages satisfied, including `reference_readiness`.
- Binance `BTCUSDT.BINANCE` is present in the NT cache or the strategy reference config is changed through the accepted TOML/provider model with equivalent evidence.
- Polymarket execution account readiness is proven without relying on fake cache entries or bypassing NT provenance.
- The final run remains SSM-only for secrets and does not print secrets.

issue.title: [Deferred Ops] Developer-tool storage hygiene (codex logs/sessions, rustup toolchains)
issue.body:
## Problem

The epic body (#123) and its 2026-04-18 comment flagged "Newly Discovered Symptoms" that are not bolt-v2 product code but accumulate while doing bolt-v2 work, with no rotation/retention policy and no implementation owner. Two of them are big enough to matter:

1. **Codex telemetry has no rotation policy**
   - `~/.codex/log/codex-tui.log` — single rolling debug log. Was 1.4 GB at the 2026-04-18 audit; observed at **9.7 GB** on 2026-05-17 (truncated manually after observation). One rotation under `~/.codex/log/archive/` totaling another 4.0 GB. No size cap, no count cap, no TTL.
   - `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl` — historical session transcripts. 3.2 GB across 1054 files on 2026-05-17, 376 of them older than 14 days. No GC.
   - `~/.factory/logs/droid-log-single.log` — also flagged in #123 (was 767 MB). Same shape: single growing log, no rotation.

2. **Rustup toolchains accumulate without a pin-driven purge**
   - `~/.rustup/toolchains/` was 3.5 GB of ancient pinned versions (`1.56.0`, `1.57.0`, `1.65`, `1.83.0`) in the original audit. On 2026-05-17: `1.94.1` (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`), `1.95.0` (active), `stable` are all installed, totaling 4.3 GB. No automatic cleanup when the pin changes or when a no-longer-referenced toolchain has been idle past N days.

Both belong to "machine-level developer-tool hygiene that affects bolt-v2 disk pressure" — distinct subsystem from the rust-verification wrapper, distinct mechanism (config + scheduled cleanup) from the wrapper-hardening work.

## Expected Outcome

When merged:

- `~/.codex/log/codex-tui.log` is capped at a configured size with N retained rotations (e.g. 200 MB cap, 2 rotations) and cannot grow unbounded.
- `~/.codex/sessions/*.jsonl` older than a configured TTL (e.g. 14 days) are pruned, with a documented dry-run / apply mode.
- `~/.factory/logs/droid-log-single.log` has the same size cap + rotation policy as codex-tui.log, or an explicit "no policy needed, growth is bounded by X" note with evidence.
- `~/.rustup/toolchains/` retention is driven by the project pin and a TTL: only the pinned version + the active version + N most-recent toolchains are retained; everything else is removed automatically or surfaced for removal.
- All three policies are documented in a single referenceable location (this issue's PR / a doc file) so operators do not have to reverse-engineer them.

## Approach Notes

### Track 1 — codex / factory log rotation

- Prefer the tool's native config if it has one (check `~/.codex/config.toml` and codex docs before adding external machinery).
- If no native config, use `newsyslog` on macOS or a launchd-scheduled truncation script.
- Apply the same shape to `droid-log-single.log` if factory does not provide native rotation.

### Track 2 — codex sessions TTL

- Add a scheduled `find ~/.codex/sessions -name '*.jsonl' -type f -mtime +N -delete` (or equivalent) with dry-run default.
- Surface the policy and TTL in the same place as Track 1.

### Track 3 — rustup toolchain hygiene

- Read the project pin from `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- Compare against `rustup toolchain list`.
- Remove any non-pinned, non-active toolchain whose last access is older than N days, OR surface the list for confirmation.

Non-goal: blanket `~/.npm` / Homebrew / Xcode DerivedData cleanup. Those are machine-level concerns not specific to bolt-v2 and are explicitly out of scope per the scope-tightening comment on the epic.

## Risks

- **Log truncation:** removing rotation history could lose useful debugging context. Mitigate by keeping at least 2 rotations and documenting where to find them.
- **Sessions TTL:** deleting old sessions could break "look up what we did N weeks ago" workflows. 14 days is a starting point — make TTL configurable, default conservative.
- **Toolchain removal:** removing an in-use toolchain breaks builds. Mitigate by reading the active project pin and refusing to remove the active or pinned version under any condition.

## Verification

- Track 1: truncate `codex-tui.log` to known state, run a codex session that produces logs, confirm rotation triggers at the configured size and that no more than N rotations exist.
- Track 2: synthesize old + new `.jsonl` files in a scratch dir mirror, run the prune script in dry-run, confirm only the old ones are listed. Apply; confirm.
- Track 3: with `rust-toolchain.toml` pinned to `1.94.1` and an extra toolchain installed, run the hygiene check, confirm the extra is surfaced for removal and the pinned + active are not.

## Relations

Parent epic: #123
Promotes the "Newly Discovered Symptoms" sections #1 (AI Tooling Telemetry) and #2 (Obsolete Rustup Toolchains) from prose to tracked work
Distinct from: #48, #124, #125, #286, the wrapper-hardening sibling issue (all are bolt-v2 / rust-verification specific; this issue is general developer-tool hygiene)
Explicitly out of scope: general system caches (`~/.npm`, Homebrew, Xcode DerivedData) — not bolt-v2 specific, see scope-tightening comment on #123

issue.title: Define controlled Polymarket broad-discovery mode
issue.body:
## Purpose

Preserve the useful idea from PR #279 without reviving its stale implementation: Polymarket broad discovery may be needed later, but it must be an explicit, bounded, audited mode rather than an accidental side effect of enabling all-market discovery.

Current Bolt-v3 should remain fail-closed: configured-market mode must only admit the exact current/next markets derived from TOML-backed market identity. A future broad-discovery slice should define how to expand beyond that safely.

## Background

PR #279 contained old Polymarket selector proof tests around prefix discovery, transitive overlap coalescing, selector snapshot expiry, refresh interval guards, and overflow rejection. Those tests target the old `src/clients/polymarket.rs` path and are not portable to current `main`, which uses the Bolt-v3 provider binding path and `MarketSlugFilter` wiring.

The concept remains useful: if we later allow broad discovery, the implementation needs tight controls and proof that it cannot silently widen into every Polymarket market.

## Required shape

- Add broad discovery only as an explicit config mode, separate from today's narrow configured-market path.
- Require bounds in config: provider, market family, asset/cadence or equivalent scope, expiry window, max admitted markets, refresh interval, and rate limits.
- Fail closed when any bound is missing, invalid, too wide, or inconsistent.
- Preserve current narrow-mode guards: no accidental `subscribe_new_markets = true` escape hatch, no ad-hoc missing-instrument Gamma loads outside the configured plan.
- Produce operator/audit evidence: what was searched, what was admitted, what was rejected, and why.
- Prove stale discovery snapshots age out and cannot keep obsolete markets live.
- Prove overlapping discovery windows are coalesced or deduplicated so Gamma/query work does not multiply unnecessarily.
- Prove refresh intervals are strictly shorter than the shortest admitted snapshot lifetime.
- Prove overflow and extreme time-window inputs fail before query construction.

## Out of scope

- Porting PR #279 directly.
- Reintroducing old `src/clients/polymarket.rs` prefix-selector architecture.
- Weakening current Bolt-v3 configured-market fail-closed behavior.
- Live orders, capital movement, or production deploys.

## Acceptance

This issue is complete when current-main Bolt-v3 has a documented and tested broad-discovery mode whose config bounds, admission rules, audit evidence, stale-snapshot behavior, overlap handling, refresh guards, and fail-closed behavior are all covered by focused tests.

## References

- Superseded reference PR: #279
- Relevant current-main intent: keep narrow configured-market mode bounded while preserving a path for intentional controlled broad discovery later.

issue.title: Epic: CI speed, private-repo cost, and remote verification topology
issue.body:
## Objective

Make `bolt-v2` private without letting CI, Cargo, or runner cost become the development bottleneck.

Concrete target state:

- `bolt-v2` stays private.
- Agents do not use the local machine as a Rust test/compile runner; local work is limited to negligible metadata/text checks only when unavoidable.
- Development does not depend on sequential CI queues. Cost is controlled by avoiding unnecessary broad jobs, not by making developers wait in line.
- Draft/iteration commits do not launch broad managed-heavy Rust CI by default.
- Rust compile/test discovery uses small targeted remote Rust Probe jobs.
- Full CI is reserved for exact-head proof: ready PRs, explicit final `just verify-remote`, main, and tag/deploy paths.
- GitHub Actions storage/artifact spend is controlled under #700.
- Ubicloud runner minutes are reconciled to actual dollars under #714.
- The post-change rebaseline proves the private repo can operate in a manageable monthly CI cost band without making CI or Cargo the speed limit for development.

## Current Operating Model

The path to the objective is to stop creating broad CI work during iteration:

1. **Draft / iteration:** targeted remote Rust Probe for Rust compile/test discovery; no local Rust test/compile loop.
2. **Final proof:** exact-head full CI through ready PRs, explicit final `just verify-remote`, or main/tag proof paths.
3. **Private GitHub cost:** control artifact/storage growth separately from runner minutes.
4. **Ubicloud cost:** reconcile runner-minute reports to actual billing before claiming dollar targets.
5. **No queue-based workflow:** provider queues/caps can exist as emergency guardrails, but the normal solution is fewer broad jobs and smaller targeted remote jobs.

Important boundary: `workflow_dispatch` is not all waste. Some of it is the intentional full-CI proof path for draft or oversized work. The goal is to stop using full CI as the ordinary debugging loop.

## Immediate Next Steps

Do these in order unless new evidence changes the ranking. (The original #554 backtester and #799
Rust-Probe steps are DONE — both closed; see "Foundational tasks" below.)

**Bank now — queue-independent (no merge queue required):**
1. **#933 — gate `workflow_dispatch` to iteration by default** (opt-in `full_ci=true`). Confirmed
   unshipped (`workflow_dispatch = "full"` in `ci/github-actions-runners.toml`); ~83/day full-heavy
   runs, the biggest controllable heavy driver after PR-synchronize. Update the proof wrapper in
   lockstep so `just verify-remote` still runs full.
2. **#700 — P0: GitHub Actions storage** (June net $51.49/mo; storage exploded 83k->399k GB-hours from
   ~1 GiB nextest-archive artifacts). Linux runner minutes are near net-zero; storage is the
   GitHub-side cost.

**The single biggest lever — now unblocked via Mergify:**
3. **#929 — adopt Mergify merge queue + revive the parked iteration policy.** `ready_pr` /
   `ready_for_review` defer; full heavy runs only on the queue's prospective-merge boundary. Removes
   ~89% of iteration-push heavy runs. Supersedes dead #848 (GitHub-native queue is Enterprise-only on
   private). Fail-closed: queue live + `gate` required BEFORE deferral flips on.

**Prove and tighten:**
4. **#714 — P0: Ubicloud dollar reconciliation** (today sampled-only ~$142-193/mo heavy; no invoice
   access — the dollar-truth gap).
5. **#849 — P1: reduce post-merge CI to smoke + suppress redundant runs** (depends on the queue).
6. **#850 — P1: rebaseline and prove the realized savings** (#933 + #889/#892 + #929 net).

## Foundational tasks — DONE

- **Backtester draft deferral (#554):** CLOSED — always-present gate + draft-stage managed-heavy
  deferral shipped.
- **Rust Probe default debug loop / full-CI-proof-only (#799, #741):** CLOSED — wrapper hardened
  (#741 vs PR #747) and routing guidance shipped (#799).

## Current Critical Path Children

Open — the path to the target cost band:
- [ ] #933 — Gate `workflow_dispatch` to iteration by default. Queue-independent; ~83/day. NEW.
- [ ] #700 — P0: GitHub Actions storage spend ($51/mo, exploding). Queue-independent.
- [ ] #934 — Migrate deprecated `ubicloud-standard-4` heavy runner label before the pricing cutover (~+60% hike risk). Queue-independent.
- [ ] #929 — Adopt Mergify merge queue + revive iteration-policy deferral (supersedes #848, revives #872). Biggest lever.
- [ ] #714 — P0: Ubicloud billing / dollar reconciliation (sampled-only today).
- [ ] #849 — P1: Reduce post-merge CI to smoke subset + suppress redundant runs (needs the queue).
- [ ] #850 — P1: Rebaseline cost and prove the realized savings.

Closed / superseded:
- [x] #554 — Backtester CI gate + draft-stage managed-heavy deferral.
- [x] #799 — Rust Probe default-debug-loop / full-CI-proof-only guidance.
- [x] #741 — Rust Probe wrapper hardening (vs PR #747).
- [x] #848 — GitHub-native merge queue. Enterprise-only on private -> superseded by #929 (Mergify).
- [x] #887 — Draft-iteration CI cost discipline (operator policy). MERGED.
- [x] #889 — Rightsize mechanical CI jobs github-hosted -> std2. MERGED.
- [x] #892 — Fold fmt-check into clippy. MERGED.

Related follow-ups (open, non-blocking):
- [ ] #927 — single-source cheap-lane guard script discovery (#924 follow-up).
- [ ] #928 — sccache shared cache + per-worktree CARGO_TARGET isolation (#896 deferred).

## Consolidated Tail Items (closed & folded here 2026-06-18)

These were individual open issues. To stop the CI backlog becoming an unread laundry list they are now **closed and tracked here as bullets** — each retains its essential remaining work, so nothing is dropped. Re-open or pick any of them up from this list. The two P0 cost objectives (#700, #714) remain as separate open critical-path children above; these tail items are measurement/polish, not blockers.

Measurement / cost re-baseline:
- [x] #344 — Post-stack CI minute re-baseline; items 1-4 delivered, only the monthly minute measurement remains (overlaps #729).
- [x] #729 — Post-#702 fingerprint reuse-effectiveness measurement + heavy-minute re-baseline (window is current ~2026-06-18): record reuse hit-rate and before/after heavy-minutes.
- [x] #745 — Measure post-force-cancel `workflow_dispatch` billed minutes after the 14-day clean window opens 2026-06-29; compare against the #728 baseline (3,944 min).
- [x] #749 — Queue-wait observability: compute `started_at - created_at` per job in `scripts/ubicloud_runner_minutes.py`, tier-grouped summary, active-queue detection.

Verifier / hook hardening (mostly P3):
- [x] #372 — Prebuilt-tool verifier edge cases: gap #1 (indirect `bash -c cargo install` bypass) is live at `scripts/verify_ci_workflow_hygiene.py:2337`; confirm or replace the dropped ZIGBUILD / `archive.sha256` checks (gaps #2/#3/#5).
- [x] #405 — Verifier false-positive: `uses: taiki-e/install-action@<sha>` inside a `run: |` block is mis-bucketed (`verify_ci_workflow_hygiene.py:8975`) — fix or document the accepted limitation (no live workflow trips it today).
- [x] #655 — Profile + content-hash skip-cache for CPU-heavy static verifier lanes (only the #653 serialization fix landed, via PR #654).
- [x] #659 — Hook owner-resolution for nested non-workspace crates (after-edit lint silently lost); the actual fix lives in claude-config `lib/rust_verification.py` + the lint/commit hooks — bolt-v2 is only the repro anchor (P3).
- [x] #684 — Audit / loud-warn local Rust bypass vectors (`rustup run`, absolute-path cargo, cross-repo `--manifest-path`); add a disk-report/cleanup `just` recipe and BTE local-refusal tests.
- [x] #81 — One-line `justfile:447` skip-message reword (still says "— skipping" while checks continue). P3 cosmetic.
- [x] #484 — Standing trigger-based revisit tracker for the #466 verifier-decomposition decisions; the protocol lives in `specs/466-decompose-disk-governance-verifiers/evidence.md` and only acts when a trigger (bug/drift/maintenance/boundary/split/operator) fires.

Test fixture / debug-loop hygiene:
- [ ] #837 — Positive validation fixture coherence: prevent one-dimensional fixture edits (asset/source/catalog keys) from surfacing stale dependent fields one remote full-CI cycle at a time; add focused diagnostics or fixture builders so ordinary fixture mismatches are discovered before `just verify-remote` proof.

CI-workflow structure:
- [x] #356 — Duration-aware nextest shard balancing (currently a hardcoded `for shard in 1 2 3 4`, `ci.yml:505`); document the balance policy and measure within-tolerance shard durations on 2+ runs.
- [x] #681 — Ready-PR `verify-remote` has no `workflow_dispatch` fallback for stacked PRs (base ≠ main) (`scripts/rust_verification.py:3858`); add the fallback and update AGENTS.md to drop the throwaway-PR workaround.
- [x] #750 — Add explicit `timeout-minutes` to each job in `ci.yml` / `backtester-ci.yml` (none today); size from observed durations and keep the policy in config, not magic literals.
- [x] #811 — Split `scripts/ci_provenance.py` (policy input) out of crate-change detection (`backtester-ci.yml:140`); update the verifier enforcement (`verify_ci_workflow_hygiene.py:8855`) in lockstep.

## Completed CI Topology Children

- [x] #343 — Baseline measurement.
- [x] #342 — Fast source-fence / verifier lane.
- [x] #332 — Parallel clippy/test lanes.
- [x] #203 — Workflow hygiene and defense-in-depth cleanup.
- [x] #335 — GitHub Actions minute reduction via safe path filtering.
- [x] #250 — Build/tool/cache decomposition parent.
- [x] #365 — Pinned prebuilt tool installs.
- [x] #367 — Remove duplicate aarch64 compile pass.
- [x] #205 — Avoid duplicate full test/build for same-SHA smoke tags.
- [x] #195 — Preserve nextest artifacts/cache across warm reruns.
- [x] #355 — Cancel superseded PR runs.
- [x] #357 — Remove NT post-stop waits from slow tests.
- [x] #366 — Share Cargo registry/git cache without unsafe target-dir mixing.
- [x] #359 — Build-required detector precision audit.
- [x] #340 — Neutral Rust verification config path.
- [x] #358 — Dependency feature graph investigation / no local high-value trim.
- [x] #368 — Final #250 cold/warm timing proof.
- [x] #370 — no-mistakes local duplicate-test gate.
- [x] #400 — Restore-key fallback + source-fence/archive decoupling.
- [x] #648 — Ubicloud runner spend governance under remote-first verification.
- [x] #670 — Lever A fingerprint test-result reuse implementation.
- [x] #706 — Manual targeted Rust Probe primitive.
- [x] #719 — Cancel obsolete ready PR runs while preserving draft/full split.
- [x] #728 — workflow_dispatch full-CI rerun cancellation work.
- [x] #739 — Local source-fence verifier serialization diagnosis.
- [x] #740 — Lane-aware local verification scheduler.
- [x] #742 — Agent-facing verification routing, folded into local scheduler guidance.
- [x] #748 — nextest archive fan-out topology fix.
- [x] #922 / #925 — stop heavy lanes re-running on no-code PR events (edited/reopened -> noop). MERGED via #925.
- [x] #899 / #923 — nextest fingerprint-reuse completeness; fail-closed git-tree digest. MERGED via #923.

## Acceptance

This epic is complete only when:

- draft iteration does not launch broad managed-heavy Rust CI by default;
- full CI remains exact-head proof and still fails closed on missing/stale/failed evidence;
- targeted Rust Probe is the normal remote debug path, not merge proof;
- private-repo Actions storage is controlled and monitored under #700;
- Ubicloud runner minutes are reconciled to actual billing under #714;
- a post-change rebaseline shows the private repo can operate inside the intended cost band without moving heavy Rust back local;
- every open child above is either closed, explicitly superseded, or intentionally left as non-blocking maintenance with a linked rationale.

Historical sequencing and detailed evidence are preserved in the issue timeline comments. This body is the current source-of-truth map as of 2026-06-23.

issue.title: Epic: NT-first backtesting, research analytics, and dashboard implementation
issue.body:
## Purpose

Single parent epic for NT-first backtesting, research analytics, dashboard, and durable data follow-up.

BTE is not missing. NautilusTrader remains the backtest engine. Bolt should only provide the thin glue NT does not provide: strategy wiring, config overlays, feed/catalog binding, domain-specific lineage, dashboard read models, and operational capture durability.

## Decisions

- Default BTE/RA path must not require source-proof acceptance, readiness ledgers, Artifact Index commits, accepted-run-spec ceremony, PMXT/BTE task gates, or prove-before-run workflow.
- Those artifacts may remain as audit/reference tools, not default gates.
- Live trading, secrets, submit approval, and operator safety remain fail-closed.
- #637 / BTE-022 is owned elsewhere and is not part of this cleanup.
- S3/data durability is real ops work, but it is not another BTE and is not a first-P/L blocker unless the needed history only exists in local live spools.
- Maker-specific work is outside this epic.

## Evidence

- Current BTE uses NT backtesting primitives and already has the production taker strategy wired on main.
- Current BTE/RA contracts still carry source-proof / accepted-object / promotion ceremony as default contract shape.
- Current live capture/lake plumbing is local-oriented: `catalog_fs_protocol = "file"`, `rotation_kind = "none"`, runtime `RotationConfig::NoRotation`, and `lake_batch` rejects URI-style paths.
- RA already uses NT primitives where it should: `ParquetDataCatalog`, `DataBackendSession`/Arrow, and `PortfolioAnalyzer`/statistics.
- #832 completed the NT capability audit and approved this direction.

## Active Path

issue.title: [Deferred Ops] Inventory and cap uncovered disk-writing surfaces (bolt-v3 runtime, local CI artifacts, cargo registry steady-state)
issue.body:
## Problem

Epic #123's existing children cover every disk-pressure class that has been measured in the 2026-04 to 2026-05 audits. They do **not** cover surfaces that are known to write to disk but have never been characterized or capped:

1. **bolt-v3 runtime / no-mistakes daemon output.** The bolt-v3 production binary runs as a live trading daemon. Worktree names show evidence-ledger, decision-event, reconciliation, and recording subsystems in active development (`bolt-v3-evidence-ledger`, `bolt-v3-decision-evidence`, `bolt-v3-reconciliation-process-restart`, `bolt-v3-strategy-decision-events`). Nothing in this epic enumerates what the running daemon writes, where it writes, how fast it grows, or whether it has a retention policy.

2. **Local test / CI artifacts.** `cargo nextest`, integration test fixtures, snapshot files, and any test-side recordings may leave per-run artifacts in repo-rooted or temp paths. Volume per run and accumulation rate are uncharacterized.

3. **Cargo registry + git checkout steady-state growth.** `~/.cargo/registry` (1.7 GB on 2026-05-17) and `~/.cargo/git` (532 MB) grow as crates are added or NautilusTrader versions churn. No cap, no pruning policy.

Without a complete enumeration, "consistently no disk overflow" is not provable; any new consumer in (1), (2), or (3) can drive the disk to 100% even after all other epic children are done.

This issue is intentionally evidence-first. The acceptance criterion is a complete inventory plus a retention/rotation/cap policy per surface — not a specific implementation.

## Expected Outcome

A reviewable document (or set of issue comments) that contains, for each surface above:

- Exact paths written.
- Measured size after a representative run (live session for bolt-v3, full test suite for CI artifacts, baseline for cargo state).
- Measured growth rate over a known interval.
- A retention / rotation / cap policy.
- An owner reference (which existing or new implementation issue will enforce the policy).

Once that document exists, epic #123 covers every disk-writing surface, not only the historically observed ones.

## Risks

This issue is investigation-only and has no blast radius itself. The risk it addresses is that an uncharacterized surface keeps producing disk overflow regardless of how complete the rest of the epic is.

## Verification

- An operator can read the deliverable and answer, for any directory >1 GB under `~`, which surface produced it and what policy bounds it.
- Re-running the bolt-v3 daemon for a documented interval produces disk growth within the predicted bound.
- Running the full local test suite produces disk growth within the predicted bound.

## Relations

Parent epic: #123
Distinct from: #48, #124, #125, #286, #374, #375 (each owns a specific measured class; this issue owns the unmeasured-but-known-to-exist classes)

issue.title: P0: Define production-grade live trading readiness beyond Issue #360 tiny-canary test
issue.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage and refreshed after PR #364 advanced to `760bc6b7c76c5673dfd21a17548c4c37148475ae`.*

## Problem

Issue #360 is scoped to proving readiness for one controlled tiny-capital live-canary attempt. That is not the same as production-grade live trading readiness.

Current interpretation:

- `Issue #360 readiness`: deterministic envelope, exact-head CI, source-free review prep, T038 no-submit proof, T046 one tiny-capital canary, and immediate post-run evidence.
- `Production-grade live trading readiness`: repeated live operation with operational controls, monitoring, reconciliation, incident response, deploy/run ownership, and venue/account lifecycle proof across normal and failure paths.

This issue tracks the gap so completing #360 cannot be accidentally treated as permission for normal production trading.

## Related Work

- Parent/readiness source: #360
- Current PR slice: #364
- Broader bolt-v3 rebuild epic: #236

## Current Readiness Baseline

As of PR #364 head `760bc6b7c76c5673dfd21a17548c4c37148475ae`:

- Issue #360 local/PR package readiness is about `97/100`.
- Overall live-capital readiness is about `61/100` before approval-gated live/operator evidence.
- #360 has current-head code/docs/local verification, green CI, source-free Phase 8 helper refresh, current-head no-mistakes/T038/T046 fail-closed wrappers, a verified current bundle, and updated PR/issue handoff evidence.
- External source review quorum ran at `4708bc3667fc94232a59ea189bdb7c85b8e4a22a`; Gemini blockers were fixed in `4beb2d2591443208c2716cfdad8bb076b52c3596`, and Greptile findings were fixed in `a0b0e5ca423d9af1a4c383ac6e22d579255aa5fb` and `760bc6b7c76c5673dfd21a17548c4c37148475ae`.
- Latest Greptile re-review was skipped because the organization monthly flex usage limit was exceeded; no fresh current-head Greptile pass is claimed.
- #360 still has not run no-mistakes branch gate, T038 real SSM/venue no-submit, or T046 tiny-capital canary.
- If #360 is fully completed, overall readiness should move toward `65/100`, because it proves one controlled tiny live-canary path, not production operation.

## Gap To Close After #360

### P0 - Repeated-live safety evidence

- Multiple tiny-canary or staged live runs across approved market windows.
- Evidence that approval windows, one-shot nonces, submit caps, and replay boundaries hold over repeated operations.
- Explicit criteria for when canary sizing can increase, stay fixed, or roll back.

### P0 - Order lifecycle and venue-state confidence

- Submit, accept, fill, partial fill, reject, cancel-if-open, timeout, and venue disconnect behavior proven with artifacts.
- NT state and venue state reconciled after each run.
- Strategy behavior proven for both expected and adverse venue outcomes.

### P0 - Restart and recovery readiness

- Restart reconciliation proven after live submit/fill/cancel states.
- Process crash or restart does not duplicate orders or lose venue state.
- Single-runner lock and approval-consumption state survive restart boundaries.

### P0 - Operator controls and incident response

- Abort/panic command path documented, reachable, and rehearsed.
- Clear stop-trading conditions for data drift, venue failure, account mismatch, CI/deploy mismatch, or evidence capture failure.
- Human operator checklist for pre-run, during-run, and post-run actions.

### P0 - Observability and alerting

- Live logs/metrics/traces capture decision, submit, venue response, fill/cancel, reconciliation, and hygiene outcomes.
- Alerts exist for unexpected position, open order, rejected cancel, missing evidence, stale data, clock skew, and SSM/venue auth failure.
- Evidence retention path is defined without exposing raw secrets.

### P0 - Deploy and runtime source-of-truth

- Production runner binary, config, commit SHA, and deploy host are pinned and auditable.
- No local/manual drift between reviewed commit, deployed binary, root TOML, and operator approval artifact.
- Rollback path is defined and tested.

### P0 - Secret/account hygiene

- SSM-only secret resolution remains enforced.
- No raw secret values appear in reports, logs, issue comments, PR comments, or retained artifacts.
- Post-run scan and retention/purge policy are mandatory after every live run.

### P0 - Governance and review gates

- Exact-head CI and external reviews pass for production-readiness changes.
- Any reviewer disagreement is resolved with code/evidence or explicitly waived by the operator.
- Production-live-ready language is blocked until every checklist item here has current evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Define a production readiness checklist separate from #360 tiny-canary readiness.
- [ ] Define readiness levels after #360: tiny-canary ready, staged live ready, production live ready.
- [ ] Record exact evidence required to move from one level to the next.
- [ ] Add or link operator runbooks for repeated-live operation, abort, restart recovery, and post-run hygiene.
- [ ] Add or link tests/tooling that prove order lifecycle, restart reconciliation, single-runner protection, and approval replay resistance beyond the one-canary path.
- [ ] Add or link monitoring/alerting requirements for live operation.
- [ ] Add or link deploy provenance requirements tying reviewed commit, binary, host, root TOML, SSM manifest, and approval artifact together.
- [ ] No issue, PR, runbook, or status map claims production-grade live trading readiness until this checklist is satisfied or explicitly waived.

## Non-goals

- Do not broaden #360. #360 remains the one controlled tiny live-canary readiness proof.
- Do not run live capital from this issue directly.
- Do not bypass source-review, no-mistakes, T038, or T046 approval gates.

## Initial Triage

Category: enhancement / operational readiness
State: ready-for-human
Priority: P0

issue.title: P1: Duplicate authenticated HTTP clients required for live fee/cost data
issue.body:
## Problem

bolt-v2 is forced to create and maintain its own authenticated HTTP clients (separate from the ones owned by NT's execution clients) in order to obtain live fee rates needed for strategy decision logic.

### Specific symptoms

- `src/bolt_v3_providers/polymarket.rs:541-556` (inside `build_fee_provider`) creates a new `PolymarketClobHttpClient`:
  ```rust
  let client = PolymarketClobHttpClient::new(...)?
  Ok(Arc::new(PolymarketClobFeeProvider::new(client, ...)))
  ```
  This client is instantiated with the same credentials and configuration used by the actual execution path for the same client key.

- The `PolymarketExecutionClient` (instantiated via `PolymarketExecutionClientFactory` and registered with the LiveNode) already owns an internal `PolymarketClobHttpClient` (see `crates/adapters/polymarket/src/execution/mod.rs` in the pinned revision `7c2aafb`). This field is not exposed.

- `PolymarketExecutionClient` implements only the standard `ExecutionClient` trait from `nautilus_common`. That trait provides no mechanism to query current CLOB fee rates.

- `PolymarketClobHttpClient::get_fee_rate(token_id)` is a public method on the raw client in the pinned NT revision (`src/http/clob.rs:435`), but it is not reachable from the execution client object that bolt-v2 actually uses at runtime.

- The same pattern will be required for any other venue where bolt needs pre-submit, per-instrument or per-user live cost data (e.g. Hyperliquid’s `info_user_fees` call lives on its raw HTTP client, which is similarly encapsulated inside its execution client).

## Impact

- bolt-v2 duplicates authenticated HTTP client instances, credential handling, timeout configuration, and rate limit management for the sole purpose of feeding decision-time data (fees, and potentially other costs) to strategies.
- The decision layer (`FeeProvider`, `StrategyBuildContext`, entry/exit evaluation, readiness gates, and evidence generation) has no access to fee information that already exists inside the NT execution clients that are registered and managed by the runtime.
- This duplication will be repeated for every additional venue unless the underlying access pattern changes.

## Verification

- `build_fee_provider` in `bolt_v3_providers/polymarket.rs` still constructs its own `PolymarketClobHttpClient` rather than obtaining current fee rates from the execution client registered for the same `client_key`.
- There is no public method on `PolymarketExecutionClient`, nor on the `ExecutionClient` trait it implements, that provides access to live fee rates from the CLOB in the pinned NT revision `7c2aafb30fb143069c915a3f2057bb12174405f6`.

## Related context

This problem is related to, but distinct from, the coupling issues identified in the Phase 9 audit finding F11. Even if the direct wiring from archetypes were cleaned up, the need to duplicate authenticated clients would remain because the required live data is not available through the execution clients that bolt registers.

issue.title: P0: Track Polymarket V2 adoption blockers before live enablement
issue.body:
## Summary

Polymarket CTF Exchange V2 is not ready for Bolt adoption yet. A compatibility probe against NautilusTrader `polymarket-v2` proved the compile drift is manageable, but production adoption is blocked by upstream readiness, toolchain, collateral dependency regressions, and missing runtime validation.

## Current Decision

Wait. Do not adopt NT `polymarket-v2` or flip Bolt live Polymarket execution to V2 yet.

## Evidence From Probe

Probe branch/worktree: `.worktrees/probe-nt-polymarket-v2-compat`

- NT `polymarket-v2` HEAD: `b4b2c4b7672219be56da9dfa89e7d65d094f59a4`
- NT `develop` HEAD at probe time: `0f04a8d9e6876f038ac1ea68107f9405ef3906bf`
- `polymarket-v2` had not landed on `develop`
- Bolt compiled against the V2 SHA after mechanical drift fixes
- Polymarket bootstrap/catalog/filter tests passed in the probe
- `cargo test --lib` still had 4 failures from Binance secret handling caused by the all-crate Nautilus rev bump

## Blockers

1. NT `polymarket-v2` has not landed on `develop` and was described upstream as still needing testing/user feedback.
2. Bolt adoption requires Rust `1.95.0`; CI/cross-build runners must be verified before bumping.
3. All Nautilus crates must rev together, and that currently introduces Binance secret parsing regressions.
4. PMCT / USDC-onramp support is not covered by the NT V2 adapter probe.
5. No V2 live or testnet order has round-tripped end-to-end from Bolt.
6. New NT Polymarket data config defaults are absorbed by `Default`, but Bolt should make an explicit config-backed decision before production use.

## Required Acceptance Criteria

- NT Polymarket V2 lands on NautilusTrader `develop` or another stable upstream SHA is explicitly accepted.
- Bolt toolchain and CI are upgraded to Rust `1.95.0` cleanly.
- Nautilus rev bump is applied across all `nautilus-*` crates.
- Cargo.lock churn is reviewed.
- Binance secret parsing regressions are fixed or explicitly accepted with updated tests.
- Polymarket V2 config drift is handled explicitly in Bolt config/validation, not as hidden runtime behavior.
- PMCT / USDC-onramp requirement is resolved or documented as unsupported.
- At least one controlled V2 order path is validated before live enablement.
- No live V2 execution is enabled by compile success alone.

## Out Of Scope

- Do not patch this into Slice 9 / PR #247.
- Do not adopt the current `polymarket-v2` branch SHA in production by default.
- Do not implement a local V2 signer in this issue unless explicitly scoped later.
- Do not add SDK dependencies; NT founder confirmed NT will continue direct API integration.

## Priority

P0 because Polymarket V2 is a hard external migration path for future live Polymarket execution, but the correct immediate action is controlled tracking and readiness gating, not premature adoption.

issue.title: Postmortem: Stop unsupported Bolt-v3 architecture assertions
issue.body:
## Purpose

This issue replaces the earlier postmortem text because the first version was polluted by unsupported architectural assertions.

The failure was not only an implementation mistake. The failure was that the assistant/CTO role kept speaking as if uncertain architecture decisions were settled facts.

That is not acceptable for Bolt-v3.

This issue records the corrected postmortem: what is actually known, what was wrongly asserted, why the current row 16 work stopped, and what process must change before any further implementation continues.

## Core Failure

The core failure was unsupported assertion.

The assistant repeatedly converted incomplete understanding into recommendations, task lists, roadmap claims, and implementation prompts.

Examples of bad behavior:

- Naming providers, strategies, and roles as if they were settled product architecture.
- Treating Binance as a reference-data provider concept rather than only a possible provider implementation.
- Treating Polymarket as an execution architecture rather than only a possible provider implementation.
- Treating current fixtures as architecture.
- Treating docs/status rows as authoritative even when the product intent was broader and the code shape was not proven.
- Suggesting risk-gate ownership without verifying whether that was Bolt-v2 legacy thinking or a real Bolt-v3 requirement.
- Proposing implementation directions before understanding the domain model deeply enough.
- Allowing merged-PR momentum to substitute for architectural proof.

The user’s repeated instruction was clear: Bolt-v3 must be dynamic and systematic from the start. It must not begin with a hardcoded happy path and generalize later.

That instruction was not enforced strongly enough.

## Correct Product Intent Stated By User

The product intent, as stated by the user, is:

- Bolt-v3 should not be narrowly scoped to Binance.
- Bolt-v3 should not hardcode Binance, even in policy or examples that become architecture.
- Bolt-v3 should not hardcode current concrete providers, markets, or strategies in core.
- One working strategy is only proof that the system works; it is not the architecture limit.
- After one strategy works, scaling to tens of strategies across tens of markets should be easy.
- Scaling further to hundreds of strategies across hundreds of markets should also be straightforward, without core rewrites.
- No happy-path architecture first; the systematic/dynamic solution is required from the start.

Any assistant, implementer, or reviewer must treat this as the acceptance bar.

## What Is Actually Known

Known source-of-truth facts at the time of this issue:

- Active Bolt-v3 feature baseline: `origin/feat/236-bolt-v3-slice-8-1-baseline`
- Baseline commit: `a4d169e23df76e7e47fcb1620626af5563f06347`
- Recent merged PRs into that baseline:
  - `#275`: runtime literal verifier hardening
  - `#276`: credential log provider binding
  - `#277`: NautilusTrader `v1.226.0` pin bump / peeled commit `38b912a8b0fe14e4046773973ff46a3b798b1e3e`
- The attempted row 16 branch was abandoned and restored clean:
  - Worktree: `/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2-row16-client-registration`
  - Branch: `codex/bolt-v3-row16-client-registration`
  - HEAD/base: `a4d169e23df76e7e47fcb1620626af5563f06347`
  - No local diff reported by implementer

Known code-shape concerns that triggered the stop:

- `src/bolt_v3_adapters.rs` still uses a closed concrete provider adapter enum shape.
- `src/bolt_v3_secrets.rs` still uses concrete provider resolved-secret enum variants.
- The attempted row 16 implementation could remove some direct factory imports from client registration, but it would still rely on the closed concrete adapter model underneath.

That means row 16 could look improved locally while preserving the wrong structural dependency.


## Foundational Docs And Code To Read Before Making Claims

These references are required context before making Bolt-v3 architecture claims. They are not automatically proof that the architecture is correct; they are inputs that must be checked against the user's stated intent and the current code shape.

Foundational docs:

- `AGENTS.md`
  - Repo rules, especially scope discipline, no hardcodes, no dual paths, SSM-only secret source, no credential display, review bar, and source-of-truth rules.

- `docs/bolt-v3/2026-04-28-source-grounded-status-map.md`
  - Current source-grounded status map. Treat it as status evidence, not as product truth when it conflicts with the user's corrected intent.

- `docs/bolt-v3/2026-04-25-bolt-v3-schema.md`
  - Current schema document. Read carefully because some current-fixture language may itself need correction before being used as architecture.

- `docs/bolt-v3/2026-04-25-bolt-v3-runtime-contracts.md`
  - Runtime contract language for market selection, evidence, readiness, CLOB V2 gate, and execution-related events. Do not infer ownership boundaries from it without checking code and user intent.

- `docs/bolt-v3/2026-04-25-bolt-v3-contract-ledger.md`
  - Contract ledger, including CLOB V2 readiness status and live-capital blockers.

- `docs/bolt-v3/2026-04-28-nt-first-boundary-doctrine.md`
  - NT-first boundary doctrine. Note the distinction between full doctrine audit freshness and pin compatibility.

- `docs/bolt-v3/research/nt-pin-change/2026-04-30-nt-v1-226-pin-bump.md`
  - Evidence for the NautilusTrader `v1.226.0` pin bump and peeled commit `38b912a8b0fe14e4046773973ff46a3b798b1e3e`.

- `docs/bolt-v3/research/runtime-literals/bolt-v3-runtime-literal-audit.toml`
  - Current runtime-literal allowlist; useful for no-hardcode tooling context, not proof of architecture-level no-hardcode.

Foundational code:

- `src/bolt_v3_config.rs`
  - Current root/strategy/venue config envelopes, including `ProviderKey`, `StrategyArchetypeKey`, `VenueBlock`, `ReferenceDataBlock`, and current TOML-owned NT runtime fields.

- `src/bolt_v3_validate.rs`
  - Current startup validation dispatcher and remaining core validation policy. Must be checked for accidental provider/market/archetype ownership.

- `src/bolt_v3_providers/mod.rs`
  - Current provider registry/binding root. Useful context, but do not treat the current registry shape as settled dynamic architecture.

- `src/bolt_v3_providers/polymarket.rs` and `src/bolt_v3_providers/binance.rs`
  - Current concrete provider modules. These are implementations/fixtures unless explicitly approved as architectural concepts.

- `src/bolt_v3_adapters.rs`
  - Current adapter mapping boundary. This file is central to the stopped row 16 concern because it still encodes concrete provider adapter variants.

- `src/bolt_v3_secrets.rs`
  - Current Bolt-v3 secret resolution boundary. This file is central to the stopped row 16 concern because it still encodes concrete provider resolved-secret variants.

- `src/bolt_v3_client_registration.rs`
  - Current client registration boundary. Do not claim this can be made dynamic without checking the adapter/secrets surfaces it consumes.

- `src/bolt_v3_live_node.rs`
  - Current LiveNode assembly path. Claims about live readiness, runtime behavior, no-trade boundaries, or NT ownership must be checked here.

- `src/bolt_v3_market_identity.rs`
  - Current market-identity boundary and source-level neutrality guards. Useful context for provider/market/strategy neutrality, but not a complete architecture by itself.

- `src/bolt_v3_market_families/mod.rs` and `src/bolt_v3_market_families/updown.rs`
  - Current market-family dispatch and concrete family implementation. UpDown must not be treated as the whole architecture.

- `src/bolt_v3_archetypes/mod.rs` and `src/bolt_v3_archetypes/binary_oracle_edge_taker.rs`
  - Current archetype dispatch and concrete archetype implementation. The current archetype must not be treated as the whole architecture.

- `scripts/verify_bolt_v3_runtime_literals.py` and `scripts/test_verify_bolt_v3_runtime_literals.py`
  - Runtime-literal verifier and self-tests. Useful tooling evidence for scanned literals, not sufficient evidence for dynamic architecture.

- `scripts/verify_bolt_v3_core_boundary.py`
  - Core-boundary verification context, if present on the active baseline. Use it as one evidence source, not as a substitute for architectural reasoning.

Foundational tests and fixtures:

- `tests/fixtures/bolt_v3/root.toml` and `tests/fixtures/bolt_v3/strategies/*.toml`
  - Current fixtures. Treat concrete provider/market/strategy names here as fixtures unless user-approved as architecture.

- `tests/bolt_v3_provider_binding.rs`
  - Provider-binding test context, including current adapter/filter assumptions.

- `tests/bolt_v3_client_registration.rs`
  - Client-registration evidence. Must be checked for fixture-shaped claims.

- `tests/bolt_v3_adapter_mapping.rs`
  - Adapter mapping evidence. Must be checked for closed provider enum dependence.

- `tests/bolt_v3_market_identity.rs`
  - Market identity and source-level guard tests. Useful, but failing/purposeful guard comments or fixture references must be interpreted carefully.

External source context:

- NautilusTrader pinned source at `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/38b912a/`
  - Required when making claims about NT adapter capabilities, factories, configs, risk behavior, subscriptions, CLOB V2 support, or runtime ownership.

Minimum rule for using these references:

- First identify whether a statement is a fact, inference, assumption, or product decision.
- Then cite the exact doc/code reference if it is a fact.
- If it is an inference or product decision, do not present it as settled without user confirmation.

## What Is Not Known / Not Settled

The following must not be asserted as settled without fresh evidence and user approval:

- Whether Bolt owns risk gates beyond configuring NautilusTrader and enforcing orchestration prerequisites.
- Whether any Bolt-v2 strategy/risk behavior belongs in Bolt-v3.
- What exact provider/role/capability vocabulary Bolt-v3 should use.
- What exact adapter abstraction should exist.
- What exact subscription model should exist.
- What exact strategy/archetype names should be treated as product concepts.
- What exact market-family scope should be implemented first.
- Whether a given status-map row can be closed independently of adjacent rows.

These are open architecture questions, not implementation facts.

## Why Row 16 Was Stopped

Row 16 was stopped because the attempted implementation did not prove the required architecture.

The problem was not merely that some concrete names appeared in a test.

The deeper problem was that client registration was being changed while the upstream adapter and secret surfaces still encoded concrete providers.

As a result, the implementation risked creating a misleading claim:

> client registration is provider-owned

when the actual system still depended on a concrete provider enum underneath.

That would have been false progress.

## What Prior Work Can Still Be Treated As Useful

The following prior work may still be useful, but must not be overclaimed:

- `#275` is useful as runtime-literal verifier hardening for its declared scan universe.
- `#276` is useful for moving credential-log suppression metadata for current providers.
- `#277` is useful for proving compile/test compatibility with NautilusTrader `v1.226.0`.
- String-backed provider/archetype keys are useful, but they do not by themselves prove dynamic architecture.
- Moving some config block shapes into provider/family/archetype modules is useful, but it does not by itself prove scalable provider/market/strategy binding.

None of these prove overall no-hardcode architecture.

None of these prove live trading readiness.

None of these prove that adding many providers, strategies, or markets is easy.

## What Cannot Be Claimed Right Now

Do not claim any of the following without hard evidence:

- Bolt-v3 has no hardcoded architecture.
- Bolt-v3 provider binding is solved.
- Rows 14/15/16 are independently closable as simple cleanup.
- Client registration is truly dynamic.
- Adapter registration is generic.
- Secret projection is generic.
- Binance is the reference-data provider.
- Polymarket is the execution architecture.
- A named strategy archetype is the architecture.
- Bolt owns risk gates.
- CLOB V2 live readiness is complete.
- The system can scale to many strategies/markets without core rewrites.

## Hard Evidence Bar Going Forward

Claims must be backed by evidence.

Acceptable evidence includes:

- Exact code references.
- Exact source scans.
- Tests that fail on the architecture violation being discussed.
- Exact PR base/head/diff commands for review.
- Demonstration that adding a provider/market/strategy does not touch core runtime assembly, if that claim is made.
- Demonstration that a config with multiple strategies/markets/provider bindings works, if scalability is claimed.
- CI at the exact PR head.

Unacceptable evidence:

- “Docs say so.”
- “Tests pass” when tests only cover current fixtures.
- “Current provider registry” language used as a substitute for generic design.
- Local movement of imports without proving the underlying type dependency changed.
- Assistant confidence.

## CTO Behavior Required From Now On

A CTO-role assistant must:

- Separate facts from assumptions.
- Say when something is not known.
- Ask before naming strategies, provider roles, market roles, or risk ownership.
- Avoid generating implementation prompts when the architecture is not understood.
- Avoid turning uncertainty into roadmaps.
- Avoid treating docs as product truth when the user has corrected the intent.
- Protect the user-stated architecture as the acceptance gate.
- Stop work when a slice can only create local cleanup but not structural correctness.

A CTO-role assistant must not:

- Blurt out architecture.
- Invent scope.
- Invent product nouns.
- Normalize concrete providers as examples if those examples can become architecture.
- Treat old Bolt-v2 concepts as Bolt-v3 requirements without verification.
- Recommend more code just to create motion.

## Immediate Process Rule

Before any more provider/adapter/client-registration/secrets work:

- Do not implement.
- Do not generate a detailed implementation prompt.
- Do not claim a row can close.
- First clarify the architecture with the user using facts and explicit unknowns.

The next useful output should be an architecture clarification, not a code slice, unless the user explicitly approves implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria For Closing This Issue

This issue can close only when:

- The user agrees that the corrected postmortem accurately describes the failure.
- The team has a CTO-approved architecture framing for Bolt-v3 that is not polluted by Bolt-v2 assumptions or current fixture assumptions.
- Future implementation prompts include explicit hard-evidence requirements and do not treat concrete providers/markets/strategies as architecture unless approved.
- The abandoned row 16 implementation remains abandoned unless restarted from the corrected architecture.

issue.title: Epic: Lightweight NT update scout and Bolt-v3 pointer bump lane
issue.body:
## Summary

Build a lightweight recurring NautilusTrader update scout for Bolt-v3.

The goal is not to replace CTO judgment with a giant governance machine. The goal is to regularly detect upstream NT releases/tags, resolve them to immutable SHAs, compare them with the current Bolt-v3 pin, and produce reviewable evidence or a narrow draft pin-bump PR.

## Why this replaces #164

The old #164 NT pointer probe rollout mixed too many concerns:

- upstream tag/ref discovery
- dependency pin mutation
- Cargo.lock refresh
- semantic seam registry ownership
- safe-list governance
- branch-protection/ruleset drift detection
- required-check app identity
- canary execution
- external-review artifact enforcement
- draft PR generation

That design was technically serious, but it became its own control-plane product. The immediate product need is smaller: keep Bolt-v3 aware of NT updates and make pointer bumps easy to review without overclaiming live readiness.

## Intended Model

1. Scout lane: read-only scheduled/manual check of upstream NT releases/tags.
2. Candidate lane: narrow draft PR generator for accepted NT tags/SHAs.
3. Readiness handoff: semantic/live-readiness blockers remain separate issues, never hidden inside a pin bump.

## Hard Rules

- Never auto-merge.
- Never claim live-readiness from compile/test compatibility alone.
- Never bundle semantic readiness, provider behavior, or live-capital approval into a pointer bump.
- Always record annotated tag object SHA and peeled commit SHA when applicable.
- Every generated review prompt must state exact base branch/SHA, head SHA, diff command, and file list.
- If the workflow uses `rust_verification.py`, its `claude-config` dependency must be explicit and pinned.

## Out of Scope

- Recreating the old seam-registry governance machine.
- Branch-protection/ruleset control-plane drift enforcement.
- External-review artifact status automation.
- Polymarket V2 live-readiness closure.
- Chainlink/reference-data readiness closure.
- Any live trading behavior.

## Children

Native child issues track the slices.

issue.title: Bolt-v3 ops: enforce EC2 host lifecycle and cleanup discipline
issue.body:
Parent: #236

## Problem
We found multiple Bolt-related EC2 instances left around from separate operational workstreams:

- original Polymarket host
- forensic helper host
- replacement/candidate validation host
- trusted launch/cutover host
- older data collector host

At least three were running at the same time before we stopped them on 2026-05-02. That is not the intended steady state for pre-launch Bolt-v3.

## Required outcome
Create an explicit EC2 lifecycle policy for Bolt-v3 launch and pre-launch validation hosts:

- one owner and purpose per instance
- creation reason recorded in tags
- cleanup deadline or retention reason recorded in tags
- temporary/candidate/forensic hosts stopped or terminated after their task completes
- EIP retention policy documented separately from instance lifecycle so we can keep the same IP without keeping compute alive
- read-only inventory command documented for future audits

## Current operational decision
Do not release Elastic IPs. We should keep the same IP for launch continuity.

## Acceptance criteria
- There is a documented lifecycle checklist for Bolt-v3 EC2 hosts.
- Every Bolt-v3 EC2 host has enough tags to answer: owner, purpose, created-for issue, cleanup policy, and whether EIP retention is required.
- Temporary helper/candidate hosts cannot remain running without an explicit retained-running reason.
- The epic references this issue as the EC2 lifecycle/cleanup follow-up.

issue.title: Bolt-v3 readiness: tighten typed builder boundary ergonomics and direct failure fixtures
issue.body:
Parent epic: #236
Related readiness contract: #294
Follow-up from PR #295.

## Problem

PR #295 adds the first library-level Bolt-v3 startup readiness-check slice and separates LiveNodeBuilder construction failures from final LiveNode build failures. The implementation is merge-safe, but review identified a small set of follow-up items around typed boundary ergonomics and direct failure fixtures that should be handled together rather than fragmented.

## Scope

- Decide whether `BoltV3LiveNodeBuilderError` should remain an enum for future variants or be collapsed to a struct/newtype wrapper around the NT source error.
- If a future Bolt-v3 config path can deterministically fail builder construction without test-only production hooks, add a readiness-level `LiveNodeBuilder: Failed` integration test.
- If a future non-test-only fixture can deterministically fail `register_bolt_v3_clients` through the readiness path, add a readiness-level `ClientRegistration: Failed` integration test.
- Optionally add a compile-time signature assertion for `make_bolt_v3_live_node_builder` so the typed public boundary stays pinned.

## Non-Goals

- Do not reopen the PR #295 readiness slice unless a real regression is found.
- Do not add test-only production hooks just to synthesize these failures.
- Do not enter connect, runner, strategy, market-selection, or order paths.
- Do not pull in #290 market-identity generalization or #292 EC2 lifecycle work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Any retained or changed `BoltV3LiveNodeBuilderError` shape has a clear reason in code/tests.
- Any added fixtures are deterministic, no-trade, and do not require provider-specific core imports.
- Readiness output remains facts-only and does not introduce aggregate launch booleans.
- Provider-leak and runtime-literal verifiers remain green.

## Notes

The current PR #295 state already documents why direct readiness-stage builder-construction failure is not synthesized: current Bolt-v3 config produces NT `Live` only, while the deterministic NT builder-construction failure uses `Environment::Backtest` at the live-node boundary test level.

issue.title: Investigate NT strategy panic propagation under one-process-per-entity shard
issue.body:
## Problem Statement

**What:** Q4 architecture locked at (b) — one process per logical trading entity, with N+ strategies running inside a single process. An unverified assumption underlies this choice: **does NautilusTrader's supervisor catch panics in strategy callbacks, or does an unhandled panic in one strategy crash the whole process?**

**Symptoms (what "crash-class" behavior looks like in each direction):**
- If NT catches → one strategy panicking is isolated; other strategies in the same process keep running; NT logs the panic with context. Crash blast radius = one strategy.
- If the process dies → one strategy panicking kills the entire entity process; all other strategies in that process stop; systemd auto-restart brings them back. Crash blast radius = one entity.

**Why it matters:**
1. Claude's round-2 dissent toward single-process-for-all-entities (shard choice (a)) cited this as a load-bearing claim. The dissent argued: if NT's supervisor catches panics, (a) is fine; if the process dies, (a)'s crash blast radius becomes unacceptable. We chose (b) anyway, but the same question affects (b)'s operational profile.
2. Operational expectation setting — "does a bad strategy kill the account, or just itself?" — is a question that should be answered before production, not discovered in production.
3. If NT catches panics: no additional work required beyond documenting the behavior.
4. If the process dies: may surface additional hardening requirements (e.g., per-strategy isolation via crash-restart scopes, channel-based supervisor shims, or a tighter Rust panic strategy choice).

## Approach

**Reasoning framework:** Empirical verification — 5 whys not appropriate here; this is a direct observation test.

**Starting points:**
- NT source: `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/crates/trading/src/strategy/core.rs`
- NT source: `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/crates/system/src/trader.rs`
- NT message bus: `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/crates/common/src/msgbus/`
- bolt-v2 existing strategies for reference: `src/strategies/*.rs`

**Key questions to answer:**
1. Does NT wrap strategy callbacks in a panic handler, or do panics propagate up the call stack?
2. If it wraps, what's the default behavior — isolate-and-continue, isolate-and-halt-strategy, or unwrap-and-crash?
3. Is the behavior configurable at the LiveNode / Trader level?
4. Does behavior differ across callback types (`on_event`, `on_data`, `on_book_deltas`, `on_order_event`, etc.)?
5. What does NT's own logging show when a panic occurs?
6. What's the relationship between Rust's `panic = "abort"` vs. `panic = "unwind"` (bolt-v2's current `Cargo.toml` has `panic = "abort"`) and NT's panic handling?

## Expected Outcome

- [ ] Clear, empirically-verified answer: does NT supervisor catch strategy panics, or does the process die?
- [ ] Per-callback-type verification (at least: `on_event`, `on_data`, `on_book_delta`, `on_order_event`, `on_position_event`).
- [ ] Effect of `panic = "abort"` vs. `panic = "unwind"` in `Cargo.toml` on NT's panic handling documented.
- [ ] Findings written to a docs file in the repo so future sessions don't re-investigate.
- [ ] Decision: does the Q4 lock require any operational additions (e.g., stricter restart policy, per-strategy crash-count alerting, a panic-catching wrapper)?

"Done" means we can answer "what happens when a strategy panics?" with reproduction-backed evidence, not reading-tea-leaves.

## Risks

- **Investigation-only, no production code changes.** Low blast radius.
- If the answer is "process dies," additional work may be needed (stricter restart policy, per-strategy crash-count tracking, possibly a panic-catching wrapper around user-code callbacks). That work would land in follow-up issues, not here.
- If NT's behavior is version-dependent, findings must pin the NT commit being tested (NT rev is pinned in `Cargo.toml`).

## Test Plan

1. Create a minimal test harness: LiveNode with 2-3 stub strategies, one of which panics deterministically.
2. Inject `panic!("test_panic_<callback>")` in each callback type, one at a time.
3. Run LiveNode in a dev/local env (no real venue connections required — use NT's backtest/mock engine if available).
4. Observe and record:
   - Process exit code (0? non-zero? SIGABRT? SIGSEGV?)
   - NT log output (does NT log the panic location and strategy ID?)
   - Behavior of the other strategies in the same process after the panic
   - Time from panic to process exit (instant abort vs. graceful shutdown)
   - systemd restart behavior if run under systemd in dev
5. Repeat across 3-5 callback types.
6. Document findings in `docs/investigations/nt-panic-behavior.md` with the NT rev pinned.

## Relations

Related to: #236 (bolt-v3 hard-reset epic — shard boundary Q4 decision carries this assumption)

Depends on: None — LiveNode harness can be minimal, no external venues required.

Blocks: Nothing currently. Findings may inform future operational hardening tasks but the Q4 lock does not require this to be resolved before implementation begins.

issue.title: Epic: Bolt-v2 hard-reset rebuild on thin NT layer
issue.body:
> **Audit refresh 2026-06-19 (#854) — current state.** The hard-reset shipped: bolt-v3 is the production path (PR #307, "route production entrypoint through bolt v3", merged 2026-05-13). The strategy/operator-artifacts monolith decomposition is tracked under epic **#522** (Track A slices #524/#526/#560/#572/#575/#583/#586/#591/#595 all merged). This epic stays **OPEN as the tracking umbrella** by design (per the 2026-06-15 comment). The genuinely-open P0 children blocking closure are **#229** (Chainlink testnet lane) and **#254** (Polymarket V2 adoption blockers); follow-up **#296** (bolt-v3 builder-boundary ergonomics) is also open. The "Problem Statement"/"Open decisions" text below is the original 2026-04 framing, retained for history.

## Problem Statement

bolt-v2 has 32,581 lines in `src/` across 62 local + 22 remote branches. The codebase accumulated tech debt during MVP iteration: dual paths (`config.rs` + `live_config.rs`), Polymarket concerns leaking into generic `src/platform/`, pure pass-through wrappers for NT adapters, `normalized_sink.rs` (1,007 lines) reimplementing `FeatherWriter::subscribe_to_message_bus`, `eth_chainlink_taker.rs` at 8,694 lines, NT crates pinned but unused (`nautilus-risk`, `nautilus-portfolio`, `nautilus-indicators`, `nautilus-backtest`, `nautilus-testkit`).

Live system is partially working. Chainlink delivery broken (#229), Polymarket aggressive BUY rejecting (#235), deploy source-of-truth broken via direct-instance hotfix (#207 P0 CODE RED). Sessions restart unexpectedly, compounding AI slop.

Decision: **hard-reset.** Default is to throw away current `src/`. Burden of proof is on keeping anything. Rebuild the thinnest possible layer over NT.

## Approach

First principles, not incremental refactor:

1. Use NT for everything NT provides. Every pinned `nautilus_*` crate either used or annotated in `Cargo.toml` explaining why pinned-but-unused.
2. No hardcodes: numeric literals in code, string identifiers for specific strategies/venues/feeds, architecture coupled to a specific strategy, test fixtures with strategy-specific keys. Any hardcode during implementation = full revert. Hard constraint.
3. Single source of truth for parameters. No dual paths.
4. Modular venues and price feeds — any strategy consumes any venue and any feed.
5. Every architectural decision locked in plan before code. 5+ layers of "why" per decision.
6. End-to-end path explicit before implementation starts.

## Locked decisions

- Hard-reset, not incremental refactor.
- Default = throw; keep only with rationale.
- Preserved infra: `deploy/`, `.github/workflows/`, `Cargo.toml` + NT patch, `justfile`, `.claude/rust-verification.toml`.
- Issues not closed in the cleanup child; new session handles.
- PR #231 stays open, not merged.
- `rust_verification.py` modularization in scope for overall refactor (not the cleanup child).
- MECE branch-cleanup rule: B1 (leave open-PR heads), B2 (strict delete — git proves content in main), B3 (archive-tag + delete — user-designated preserve), B4 (delete no-archive — superseded/abandoned).

## Open decisions (appended as resolved)

- **A1 — Parameter source of truth shape.** External-model consultation in progress.
- **A3 — Venue / price-feed abstraction shape.** External-model consultation in progress.
- **Deploy target.** Must precede Stage 1 mechanics (pre-start gate, drift detection).
- **A5 — Strategy SDK boundary.** To finalize in plan.
- **Grand-scheme end-state metrics.** Appended in plan.

## Cross-repo scope

Surfaces the refactor must consider (in-scope for this epic, beyond the cleanup child):

1. `~/Projects/Claude/claude-config/lib/rust_verification.py` (2,174 lines) — monolithic; modularization pending.
2. `~/.claude/hooks/` — ~20 hooks governing bolt-v2 operations.
3. `~/.claude/lib/bolt_rust_verification.py`.
4. Pinned NT commit `af2aefc24451ed5c51b94e64459421f1dd540bfb`.
5. Vendored NT Polymarket adapter at `patches/nautilus_trader_pinned/`.
6. `.github/workflows/nt-pointer-*.yml` — cross-repo contract.
7. claude-config #577 — trust-root snapshot stale (currently blocks `nt_pointer_probe_control_plane` test gate).
8. claude-config #565 — external trust-root validator (in flight as PR #579).
9. `bolt-v2/.claude/rust-verification.toml`.
10. `~/.claude/cache/rust-verification-registry.json`.

## Expected Outcome

Living record:

- Every decision (locked and pending) recorded with context.
- Every plan stage posted as a timeline comment with 5+ layer justifications.
- Child issues linked back to this epic.
- Post-cutover acceptance: ≥2 strategies live on ≥2 venues placing correct real orders, full queryable lake, backtest harness wired through NT `BacktestEngine`, strategy registration low-friction (target: ≥10/day).

## Risks

- Dumping ground without curation. Mitigation: comments use prefixes (`Decision:`, `Action:`, `Consult:`, `Plan:`) + dates.
- Architectural decisions made outside the issue and not recorded → record goes stale. Mitigation: every out-of-band decision copied back as a comment.
- New sessions ignore the issue and re-plan → 5+ layer-why discipline fragments. Mitigation: this issue is session-starter; sessions open it before any action.
- Timeline uncertain; issue may stay open for many sessions. Mitigation: expected.

## Test Plan

Meta-tracking issue. Validation by comment discipline:

- Every major decision posted as `Decision:` comment with date.
- Every cleanup stage posted as `Action:` comment with script reference + result.
- External consultation responses posted verbatim as `Consult:` comments.
- Plan stages posted as `Plan:` comments with 5+ layer justifications.
- Cross-references: every bolt-v2 or claude-config issue/PR touched during the refactor references this issue number.

## Children

- #229 — P0 Chainlink/reference-data correctness child task for a future Bolt-v3 reference-data slice. (OPEN)
- #254 — P0: Track Polymarket V2 adoption blockers before live enablement. (OPEN)
- #296 — Bolt-v3 readiness: typed builder boundary ergonomics + direct failure fixtures. (OPEN, comment-referenced follow-up)

## Relations

- Related to #207 (CODE RED deploy breach — refactor addresses class structurally)
- Related to #229 (Chainlink testnet; PR #231 stays open)
- Related to #235 (Polymarket aggressive BUY semantics)
- Related to #221, #222, #223, #224 (replacement-host epic — deploy target decision precedes)
- Related to #230 (Polymarket capped market — active work)
- Related to #212 (reference venue startup gate — re-done under new SDK)
- Related to seungpyoson/claude-config#565 (external trust-root validator — PR #579 in flight)
- Related to seungpyoson/claude-config#577 (trust-root snapshot refresh — currently blocking bolt-v2 test gate)
