PR #279 contained old Polymarket selector proof tests around prefix discovery, transitive overlap coalescing, selector snapshot expiry, refresh interval guards, and overflow rejection. Those tests target the old `src/clients/polymarket.rs` path and are not portable to current `main`, which uses the Bolt-v3 provider binding path and `MarketSlugFilter` wiring.

The concept remains useful: if we later allow broad discovery, the implementation needs tight controls and proof that it cannot silently widen into every Polymarket market.

## Required shape

- Add broad discovery only as an explicit config mode, separate from today's narrow configured-market path.
- Require bounds in config: provider, market family, asset/cadence or equivalent scope, expiry window, max admitted markets, refresh interval, and rate limits.
- Fail closed when any bound is missing, invalid, too wide, or inconsistent.
- Preserve current narrow-mode guards: no accidental `subscribe_new_markets = true` escape hatch, no ad-hoc missing-instrument Gamma loads outside the configured plan.
- Produce operator/audit evidence: what was searched, what was admitted, what was rejected, and why.
- Prove stale discovery snapshots age out and cannot keep obsolete markets live.
- Prove overlapping discovery windows are coalesced or deduplicated so Gamma/query work does not multiply unnecessarily.
- Prove refresh intervals are strictly shorter than the shortest admitted snapshot lifetime.
- Prove overflow and extreme time-window inputs fail before query construction.

## Out of scope

- Porting PR #279 directly.
- Reintroducing old `src/clients/polymarket.rs` prefix-selector architecture.
- Weakening current Bolt-v3 configured-market fail-closed behavior.
- Live orders, capital movement, or production deploys.

  "title": "P1: Discover grouped Polymarket World Cup event markets from match pages",
  "body": "## Problem
PR606 supports explicit `static_binary_event` targets, where each configured target maps to one exact Polymarket binary market. That is not enough for World Cup match pages such as IR Iran vs New Zealand, where one event page exposes many tradable markets: moneyline legs, spreads, totals, both-teams-to-score, first-team-to-score, team totals, halves, corners, goals, assists, shots, and other in-game props.

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE once triggered. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only when user says "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Abbreviate common terms (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl). Strip conjunctions. Use arrows for causality (X -> Y). One word when one word enough.

Technical terms stay exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

> Inline obj prop -> new ref -> re-render. `useMemo`.

**"Explain database connection pooling."**

> Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake -> fast under load.

Drop caveman temporarily for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.

> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
>
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

# Create Issue

Create a GitHub issue that can start a future session without requiring the
current chat. Keep the body concrete and reviewable.

## Steps

1. Detect repository with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner`
   unless the user provided `--repo owner/name` or named a repo.
2. Infer a complete draft from context:
   - Title
   - Problem statement
   - Expected outcome
   - Risks / blast radius
   - Test or verification plan
   - Related issues and dependencies
3. Add labels only when clear from context. Prefer existing repo taxonomy; do
   not invent large label sets.
4. Show the draft and wait for user approval.
5. Create with `gh issue create --repo <repo> --title <title> --body-file <file>`.
   Use a temp body file so user text is not shell-interpolated.
6. Link relations:
   - Put `Related to #N` / `Depends on #N` in the body for normal
     bidirectional GitHub timeline links.
   - Parent/child links are opt-in only when the user explicitly asks.
7. Confirm issue number, title, labels, related issues, and URL.

## Body Template

```markdown
## Problem
<what is wrong or missing, and why it matters>

## Expected Outcome
<observable done state>

## Approach Notes
<constraints, likely direction, and non-goals>

## Risks
<blast radius and reversibility>

## Verification
<tests, commands, or inspection required>

## Relations
Related to #<n>
Depends on #<n>
```

## Rules

- Confirm before creating.
- Do not close, relabel unrelated issues, or mutate related issues unless the
  user explicitly approves that action.
- Keep stable acceptance criteria in the issue body; put sequencing or later
  implementation notes in comments.

# GitHub

## Overview

Use this skill as the umbrella entrypoint for general GitHub work in this plugin. It should decide whether the task stays in repo and PR triage or should be handed off to a more specific review, CI, or publish workflow.

This plugin is intentionally hybrid:

- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for repository, issue, pull request, comment, label, reaction, and PR creation workflows.
- Use local `git` and `gh` only when the connector does not cover the job well, especially for current-branch PR discovery, branch creation, commit and push, `gh auth status`, and GitHub Actions log inspection.
- Keep connector state and local checkout context aligned. If the request is about the current branch, resolve the local repo and branch before acting.

Once the intent is clear, route to the specialist skill immediately and do not keep broad GitHub triage in scope longer than needed.

## Connector-First Responsibilities

Handle these directly in this skill when the request does not need a narrower specialist workflow:

- repository orientation once the repo, PR, issue, or local checkout is identified
- recent PR or issue triage
- PR metadata summaries
- PR patch inspection
- PR comments, labels, and reactions
- issue lookup and summarization
- PR creation after a branch is already pushed

Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for those flows because it provides structured PR, issue, and review-adjacent data without depending on a local checkout. If the repository is not already identifiable from the user request or local git context, ask for the repo instead of pretending there is a repo-search flow that may not exist.

## Routing Rules

1. Resolve the operating context first:
   - If the user provides a repository, PR number, issue number, or URL, use that.
   - If the request is about "this branch" or "the current PR", resolve local git context and use `gh` only as needed to discover the branch PR.
   - If the repository is still ambiguous after local inspection, ask for the repo identifier.
2. Classify the request before taking action:
   - `repo or PR triage`: summarize PRs, issues, patches, comments, labels, reactions, or repository state
   - `review follow-up`: unresolved review threads, requested changes, or inline review feedback
   - `CI debugging`: failing checks, Actions logs, or CI root-cause analysis
   - `publish changes`: create or switch branches, stage changes, commit, push, and open a draft PR
3. Route to the specialist skill as soon as the category is clear:
   - Review comments and requested changes: `../gh-address-comments/SKILL.md`
   - Failing GitHub Actions checks: `../gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md`
   - Commit, push, and open PR: `../yeet/SKILL.md`
4. Keep the hybrid model consistent after routing:
   - connector first for PR and issue data
   - local `git` and `gh` only for the specific gaps the connector does not cover

## Default Workflow

1. Resolve repository and item scope.
2. Gather structured PR or issue context through the GitHub app from this plugin.
3. Decide whether the task stays in connector-backed triage or needs a specialist skill.
4. Route immediately when the work becomes review follow-up, CI debugging, or publish workflow.
5. End with a clear summary of what was inspected, what changed, and what remains.

## Output Expectations

- For triage requests, return a concise summary of the repository, PR, or issue state and the next likely action.
- For mixed requests, tell the user which specialist path you are taking and why.
- For connector-backed write actions, restate the exact PR, issue, label, or reaction target before applying the change.
- Never imply that GitHub Actions logs are available through the connector alone. That remains a `gh` workflow.

## Examples

- "Use GitHub to summarize the open PRs in this repo and tell me what needs attention."
- "Help with this PR."
- "Review the latest comments on PR 482 and tell me what is actionable."
- "Debug the failing checks on this branch."
- "Commit these changes, push them, and open a draft PR."

Track the modular follow-on work that remains after the reduced Task 4 cut.

- PR #31 merged the reduced Task 4 `#18` batch seam

But the EC2 proof work exposed two new high-priority follow-ons before the remaining data-lake expansion tasks:
- `#32` canonical live deploy / operator drift guardrails
- `#33` NT data completeness gap in the current seam

So the next execution tasks are no longer just `#23` and `#19`.

## Phase folding

### Phase 0: deploy and completeness guardrails — DONE (2026-06-19 audit)

This phase folds together:
- [x] #32 Deploy: fail fast on invalid canonical live operator configs (closed COMPLETED, PR #43)
- [x] #33 Data lake: investigate and close NT data completeness gap in current seam (closed COMPLETED)

Why these come first now:
- `#32` addresses the deploy/runtime drift that prevented EC2 from being a trustworthy proof of current `main`
- `#33` addresses the newly exposed product gap between “the seam works” and “the seam is complete enough to match NT expectations”

What we get after Phase 0:
- a more reliable canonical deploy path
- fewer session-to-session deployment assumptions
- a clearer statement of what the seam actually captures today versus what NT can provide

### Phase 1: reduced ETL seam completion

This phase folds together:
- [x] #18 Data lake: convert NT live spool core market-data classes to local Parquet
- [ ] #23 Data lake: bridge NT instrument stream spool into normalized instruments Parquet
- [ ] #19 Data lake: attach lineage metadata to normalized lake builds

Why these belong together:
- `#18` gives the main stream-to-Parquet path for the NT-supported classes
- `#23` closes the one confirmed `instruments` gap so the reduced ETL seam is complete
- `#19` makes the reduced output reproducible and auditable instead of just usable

What we get after Phase 1:
- a complete reduced Task 4 batch seam
- local normalized Parquet for core market-data tables plus instruments
- explicit build lineage on normalized output
- no changes to the live runtime path

### Phase 2: semantic dimensions

This phase folds together:
- [ ] #22 Data lake: materialize versioned normalized_markets dimension
- [ ] #21 Data lake: materialize normalized_resolutions with provenance history

Why these belong together:
- `#22` adds the descriptive market catalog needed to understand and join the event data
- `#21` adds the outcome/resolution side needed for labels, audits, and post-market analysis
- together they form the missing semantic layer that the reduced ETL cut intentionally leaves out

What we get after Phase 2:
- versioned market metadata history
- versioned resolution history with provenance
- a research-usable semantic layer on top of the reduced normalized event tables

### Phase 3: canonical publish contract

This phase folds together:
- [ ] #20 Data lake: publish canonical normalized lake layout for Athena and DuckDB

Why this is its own phase:
- this is where reduced local Parquet output becomes a stable analytics-facing lake contract
- it depends on the lower layers existing first, especially lineage and semantic dimensions

What we get after Phase 3:
- repo-owned normalized table names and paths
- documented and validated layout for Athena and DuckDB
- a stable publish contract instead of mostly NT-native physical output

## Current execution order

Phase 0 (`#32`, `#33`) is complete; remaining open lane:

1. `#23`
2. `#19`
3. `#22`
4. `#21`
5. `#20`

## Explicitly out of this epic

- Task 1 / 2 / 3 runtime and capture redesign
- broader capture throughput hardening tracked separately in #15
- raw capture itself tracked separately in #4
- feature / label / experiment pipelines
- full S3 / Glue / broader infra expansion unless later issues explicitly add it

## What we get when this epic is complete

When this epic is done, bolt-v2 has:
- a proven offline NT-first batch seam from Task 3 spool to normalized Parquet
- coverage for the core normalized event tables and instruments
- explicit lineage on normalized builds
- versioned `normalized_markets` and `normalized_resolutions`
- a repo-owned canonical normalized lake contract validated for Athena and DuckDB
- a stronger canonical deploy/operator path with less EC2 drift
- a clearer, less surprising match between NT-available data and what the seam actually captures

In plain English: Task 1/2/3 gave us capture, reduced Task 4 gave us the first ETL seam, the EC2 proof exposed deploy/completeness gaps, and this epic now tracks both the guardrails and the remaining data-lake layers needed to make the system robust.

## Goal

Track the strategy-platform work needed to move `bolt-v2` from a single hardwired `exec_tester` lane into a practical Polymarket trading platform that starts narrow and scales additively.

The current repo has:

- one live Polymarket execution lane
- one `exec_tester` strategy kind

issue.title: [P2][Deferred Architectural] Revisit venue-contract enforcement boundary and infrastructure model
issue.body:
Background

PR #45 (`feat/33-venue-contract-clean`, head `87815849754654ff4e88079ae8eaf40b21a2907e`) deliberately froze several design choices so the implementation could converge cleanly.

This issue is for the items that are *not* straightforward hardening work. They require an explicit product / architecture decision before code changes should happen.

Questions to revisit

1. Startup vs ETL enforcement boundary
- Today startup validates the contract file, but ETL / lake conversion enforces stream policy.
- Should disabled / unsupported streams be prevented earlier at capture time?
- Should the node fail earlier instead of allowing post-hoc ETL failure?

2. Subscription pruning
- Today sink subscriptions are intentionally not pruned by contract policy.
- Should startup selectively suppress capture for disabled / unsupported streams?
- Tradeoff: earlier prevention vs preserving raw evidence of unexpected data.

3. Non-contract streams such as `bars`
- Today a non-contract stream can still be captured and later fail ETL as an unknown / violating class.
- Should that remain the intended fail-closed behavior, or should the capture boundary change?

4. Infrastructure data model
- Today `instruments/` and `status/` are treated as infrastructure and are not parquet-converted contract streams.
- Should some or all of that data be preserved in the lake as first-class outputs instead?

5. Relative-path semantics for live-local `contract_path`
- Today relative live-local `streaming.contract_path` is resolved from repo root.
- Should that remain the contract, or should resolution move to config-file-relative semantics?

Why this is separate

These are not cleanup items. They change the contract surface, operational semantics, or downstream data model.

Acceptance criteria
- Written decision for each item above (keep / change / defer)
- If behavior changes, define migration and test updates explicitly
- Do not bundle these changes implicitly into unrelated hardening PRs

issue.title: [Epic][P2] Kalshi venue integration: catalog, data capture, and execution
issue.body:
## Problem Statement

**What:** bolt-v2 is Polymarket-only. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated prediction market with USD settlement, REST + WebSocket APIs, and a different market model. Adding Kalshi as a second venue enables cross-venue arbitrage, diversifies execution risk, and exercises the multi-venue abstractions we're building (reference-price pipeline #35/#37, venue weighting #39).

**Symptoms:** No Kalshi adapter exists. Some test scaffolding references Kalshi (`src/validate/tests.rs:737`, `tests/audit_records.rs:285`) and deploy entries exist for `bolt-kalshi` / `kalshi-data-collector` instances, but no implementation.

**Why it matters:** Single-venue concentration risk. Kalshi has unique markets not available on Polymarket, and regulated USD settlement simplifies accounting.

## Approach

**Reasoning framework:** Working backwards from full parity with the Polymarket adapter — catalog discovery, market data capture, normalized lake integration, and order execution.

**Key questions to answer before implementing:**
- What does the Kalshi API look like? (REST endpoints, WebSocket streams, auth model)
- How do Kalshi market IDs/structures map to our normalized instrument model?
- Does NT have any Kalshi adapter work, or is this entirely bolt-v2 custom?
- What SSM parameters are needed for Kalshi credentials?

**Expected sub-issues (to be created as work begins):**
1. Kalshi API client — REST + WebSocket, auth, rate limits (`src/clients/kalshi.rs`)
2. Kalshi catalog ingest — market discovery, instrument normalization
3. Kalshi market data capture — orderbook + trade streams, raw capture pipeline
4. Kalshi normalized lake integration — Parquet sink, schema alignment with Polymarket lake
5. Kalshi execution adapter — order submission, fill tracking, execution state
6. Kalshi deploy config — TOML sections, SSM secrets, EC2 instance config

**Starting points:**
- `src/clients/` — add `kalshi.rs` alongside existing venue clients
- `src/platform/polymarket_catalog.rs` — pattern for catalog ingest
- `src/validate/tests.rs:737` — existing Kalshi validation scaffolding
- `tests/audit_records.rs:285` — existing Kalshi test references
- `src/config.rs` / `src/live_config.rs` — TOML config for new venue

## Expected Outcome

- [ ] Kalshi markets discoverable via catalog ingest
- [ ] Kalshi orderbook and trade data captured to raw + normalized lake
- [ ] Orders submittable to Kalshi through bolt-v2 execution path
- [ ] Kalshi venue config follows same TOML patterns as Polymarket (no dual paths)
- [ ] Existing Polymarket functionality unaffected

## Risks

- **API access:** Kalshi may require institutional onboarding or have API waitlists → verify access early
- **Market model mismatch:** Kalshi's event/market structure differs from Polymarket → normalization layer needs care
- **Scope creep:** Full venue parity is large — sub-issues keep each piece shippable independently
- **Blast radius:** New venue, additive — no risk to existing Polymarket paths if properly isolated

## Test Plan

- [ ] Kalshi client: unit tests for REST + WS message parsing
- [ ] Catalog: verify instrument normalization against known Kalshi markets
- [ ] Data capture: end-to-end test capturing live Kalshi orderbook snapshots
- [ ] Execution: testnet order submission and fill verification
- [ ] Regression: full Polymarket test suite passes unchanged

## Relations

Related to: #35 (shared reference-price pipeline), #37 (Chainlink ingest — same multi-venue pattern), #39 (venue weighting), #46 (venue-contract enforcement boundary)
Depends on: None
Blocks: None

issue.title: Follow-on: expose Gamma resolutionSource and migrate resolution_basis to structured config
issue.body:
## Problem

Issue #109 keeps `rulesets[*].resolution_basis` as a flat string and is constrained by the current Polymarket adapter seam. The upstream Gamma JSON includes `resolutionSource`, but the pinned `GammaMarket` struct used by `bolt-v2` does not expose it at runtime, so the selector path can only parse `description` today.

That means we still need a follow-on to finish the seam cleanup:

- surface `resolutionSource` on the adapter model used by `bolt-v2`
- move operator config from flat-string `resolution_basis` to structured tagged config

## Why this matters

The internal typed `ResolutionBasis` model introduced for #109 is the correct long-term seam, but leaving config as a flat string and adapter metadata partially hidden keeps two temporary constraints in place:

- config still depends on a synthetic flat-string grammar
- market parsing cannot yet compare `resolutionSource` and `description` and fail closed on structural disagreement

## Scope

This follow-on should include:

- expose `resolutionSource` on the Polymarket `GammaMarket` runtime model used by `bolt-v2`
- parse `resolutionSource` and `description` independently into the same internal `ResolutionBasis`
- merge parsed values at the typed level
- fail closed when both sides parse and disagree structurally
- migrate `rulesets[*].resolution_basis` from flat string to structured tagged TOML
- preserve the internal `ResolutionBasis` model as the source of truth so selector/runtime logic does not need another rewrite

## Proposed config target

```toml
[rulesets.resolution_basis]
kind = "exchange_candle"
source = "binance"
pair = "PAIR"
interval = "1h"
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `GammaMarket` runtime parsing exposes `resolutionSource`
- market basis parsing uses both `resolutionSource` and `description`
- structurally conflicting metadata is rejected
- operator config uses structured tagged `resolution_basis`
- selector/runtime logic continues to compare typed `ResolutionBasis` values without another seam rewrite

## Related

- blocked behind or follows #109 depending on merge order
- design context in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-resolution-basis-selector-generalization-design.md` at commit `cceb3ed`

issue.title: [Epic][Deferred Ops] Organize bolt-v2 local disk pressure, temp growth, and cache growth
issue.body:
## Summary

This epic organizes the current `bolt-v2` local disk-pressure symptom set into modular investigation tracks.

The point here is not to guess the fix in advance. The point is to keep each recurring symptom narrowly scoped while still tracking the full picture in one place.

## Why this epic exists

Recent cleanup confirmed that branch/worktree sprawl was **not** the main active disk consumer anymore.

At investigation time, the machine was at:

```text
Filesystem      Size    Used   Avail Capacity
/dev/disk3s5   460Gi   395Gi    23Gi    95%
```

The main active consumers were:

- `/private/tmp/claude-501` = `56G`
- `/private/var/folders/y5/syb9vj4n3l10028h1jst4_tm0000gn/T` = `47G`
- `/Users/spson/.cache/rust-verification/bolt-v2` = `26G`

Those are distinct symptom classes and should not be collapsed into a single vague issue.

## Child issues

Investigation tracks (symptom owners):

- [x] #48 `[Deferred Ops] Investigate Rust worktree target / disk pressure` (CLOSED 2026-06-18 — archived as the investigation/evidence record; forward work delegated to #374/#286/#124, all closed)
- [x] #70 `[Deferred Ops] Investigate multi-GB temp Cargo/home directory growth around bolt-v2 verification`
- [x] #124 `[Deferred Ops] Investigate managed rust-verification cache growth for bolt-v2`
- [x] #125 `[Deferred Ops] Investigate Claude/Codex temp output artifact growth under /private/tmp for bolt-v2`
- [ ] #376 `[Deferred Ops] Inventory and cap uncovered disk-writing surfaces (bolt-v3 runtime, local CI artifacts, cargo registry steady-state)`
- [ ] #486 `cargo build saturates CPU/RAM: 847 unique crates, no build tuning` (folded in 2026-06-18 — resource-pressure sibling)

Implementation tracks (policy/enforcement owners):

- [x] #286 `[Deferred Ops] Optimize managed Rust verification cache retention for bolt-v2`
- [x] #374 `[Deferred Ops] Wrapper hardening: shell-agnostic shim + artifact lifecycle + preflight disk gate`
- [ ] #375 `[Deferred Ops] Developer-tool storage hygiene (codex logs/sessions, rustup toolchains)`
- [ ] #377 `[Deferred Ops] Lightweight unknown-class detection layer for bolt-v2 disk pressure`
- [x] #671 `Make cargo-shim installer shell-neutral and self-verifying` (Phase 2 of the #374 shim; closed & folded 2026-06-18)

## Scope boundaries

- `#48` — history/evidence record for the worktree/lineage/local-target symptom class. Gap 1 and Gap 2 implementation moved to `#374`; Gap 3 owned by `#124`/`#286`.
- `#70` — Rust/Cargo/macOS temp-tree growth outside the canonical managed target root. Closed as resolved-by-investigation.
- `#124` — canonical managed rust-verification cache symptom track.
- `#125` — Claude/Codex session-output artifacts under `/private/tmp/claude-*`. Phase 1 containment shipped.
- `#286` — implementation track for `#124`: retention/pruning policy + enforcement of soft limit.
- `#374` — implementation track for `#48` Gap 1/Gap 2: shell-agnostic cargo shim + worktree/tmp lifecycle sweep + preflight disk gate.
- `#375` — codex log rotation, codex sessions TTL, rustup toolchain hygiene. Promotes "Newly Discovered Symptoms" sections #1 and #2 below from prose to tracked work.
- `#376` — characterize and cap surfaces never measured: bolt-v3 daemon runtime output, local CI/test artifacts, `~/.cargo/registry` + `~/.cargo/git` steady-state growth.
- `#377` — unknown-class detection layer, independent of cargo entry (complements `#374`'s preflight, not a duplicate).
- `#486` — cargo/rustc build-time CPU + RAM saturation (build tuning: `.cargo/config.toml` job caps, mold linker, `[profile.dev]` split-debuginfo, sccache). Resource-pressure sibling to the disk-pressure tracks; folded here 2026-06-18.
- `#671` — Phase 2 of the `#374` cargo shim. Closed & folded 2026-06-18; remaining work preserved here: write a POSIX `/bin/sh`-valid env snippet, convert the `.zshenv` block to a small adapter sourcing it (drop the zsh-only `unfunction`), add a `--check` read-only doctor mode with nonzero exit on stale/missing state, plain-English operator docs, and tests for `--check` / POSIX snippet / `.zshenv` adapter / stale-shim detection.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each major recurring disk-pressure symptom has a focused child issue.
- Each child issue contains exact measured paths and current evidence.
- Root-cause investigation and fixes can be split without scope confusion.
- Cleanup/retention/preflight policy decisions can be attached to the right symptom bucket.


## Newly Discovered Symptoms (April 2026 Audit)

During a deep workspace investigation, additional massive sources of disk pressure were discovered that were previously untracked in this epic.

### 1. Unmanaged AI Tooling Telemetry and Transcripts (~2.9 GB)
> Now tracked under `#375` (codex log rotation + sessions TTL + droid log).

While #125 covers runaway `.output` spools in `/private/tmp/claude-*`, it missed the permanent telemetry logs and historical sessions accumulating in the user's home directory.

**Evidence:**
- `~/.codex/log/codex-tui.log` (**1.4 GB**): Active, rolling application debug log for the terminal tool. Never truncated.
- `~/.factory/logs/droid-log-single.log` (**767 MB**): Resource monitoring telemetry log.
- `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl` (**~750 MB**): Stale JSON transcripts of historical AI sessions (e.g., from weeks ago) that are never garbage collected.

**Reproducible Process to Investigate:**
1. Check `du -sh ~/.codex/log/codex-tui.log ~/.factory/logs/droid-log-single.log`
2. Check total size of stale sessions: `find ~/.codex/sessions -name "*.jsonl" -type f -exec du -ch {} + | grep total`

### 2. Obsolete Rustup Toolchains (~3.5 GB)
> Now tracked under `#375` (rustup toolchain hygiene policy).

While #70 and #124 focus on Cargo build artifacts and verification caches, the `~/.rustup/toolchains/` directory had accumulated multiple ancient compiler versions taking up roughly **3.5 GB**. Since the project pins to `1.94.1` (via `rust-toolchain.toml` and CI workflows), these are dead weight.

**Evidence:**
- `~/.rustup/toolchains/1.56.0-aarch64-apple-darwin` (417 MB)
- `~/.rustup/toolchains/1.57.0-aarch64-apple-darwin` (427 MB)
- `~/.rustup/toolchains/1.65-aarch64-apple-darwin` (437 MB)
- `~/.rustup/toolchains/1.83.0-aarch64-apple-darwin` (1.2 GB)

**Reproducible Process to Investigate:**
1. List installed toolchains: `rustup toolchain list`
2. Check size: `du -sh ~/.rustup/toolchains/*`
3. Compare against `rust-toolchain.toml` and `.github/workflows/`

### 3. General Developer System Caches (~1.8 GB)
> **Out of scope for this epic.** Machine-level, not bolt-v2 specific. Track on the machine/dev-environment config repo, not here.

Untracked system-level package manager caches that collect dust over time and cause silent disk pressure.

**Evidence:**
- `~/.npm` (**913 MB**)
- `~/Library/Caches/Homebrew` (**565 MB**)
- `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData` (**340 MB**)

**Reproducible Process to Investigate:**
1. Check sizes: `du -sh ~/.npm ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`

issue.title: Epic: ETH 5m Chainlink adaptive taker — corrected minimum path (supersedes #130 Phase 3 chain)
issue.body:
> **Audit refresh 2026-06-19 (#854) — relabel, kept OPEN.** The ETH-5m-Chainlink-specific framing below is **superseded** by the broader bolt-v3 binary-taker architecture. The production artifact is **`src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/`** (present at HEAD); the originally-named target `src/strategies/eth_chainlink_taker.rs` was discarded in the #236 hard-reset and does not exist. Children: **#134 COMPLETED**, **#136 COMPLETED**, **#135 closed (superseded** — the ETH-5m strategy kind folded into the generic taker; stateReason NOT_PLANNED). This epic stays **OPEN** because its core acceptance criterion — a first supervised live profit-seeking run on `eth-updown-5m-*` with one capped order at honest EV, resolving cleanly — is **still unproven** (live-pilot work tracked under #630/#633). The text below is the original 2026-04 framing (anchored at `main@005d489`), retained for history.

## Problem Statement

**What:** `bolt-v2` cannot run any profit-seeking strategy today. Strategy kind is hardcoded to `exec_tester` (a `nautilus_testkit::testers::ExecTester` order-placement test harness) at five independent enforcement points. The previous Phase 3 decomposition (#118 → #126 → #129 → #110 → #132, tracked in epic #130) produced two closed PRs (#128, #131) without landing a real strategy and is not the minimum-interruption path. This epic defines the corrected minimum path: two ordered issues that enable a rotating ETH 5m Chainlink adaptive taker strategy against live Polymarket `eth-updown-5m-*` markets.

**Symptoms:**
- `main@005d489` strategy runtime accepts only `kind == "exec_tester"`. Any other kind is rejected at config load (`src/validate.rs:668,1259-1265`), at startup (`src/main.rs:162-173`), or silently filtered in ruleset mode (`src/platform/runtime.rs:627-642`). Ruleset-mode validation requires exactly one `exec_tester` template (`src/validate.rs:1442-1458`). The strategies module exposes only `exec_tester` (`src/strategies/mod.rs:1`).
- Ruleset mode destroys and recreates the managed strategy on every market switch, idle, or freeze (`src/platform/runtime.rs:677-756`). Strategy-local state (interval-open price, warmup counter, cooldown ledger, recovery flag, one-position invariant) would be lost every 5 minutes. Current tests explicitly encode this replacement behavior (`tests/platform_runtime.rs:879,936,1009`).
- Current candidate loader returns a raw CLOB token id with no `.POLYMARKET` suffix (`src/platform/polymarket_catalog.rs:100,118-123`). NT `InstrumentId::from_str` panics on first `Active` ruleset decision without the venue suffix (`nautilus_trader/crates/model/src/identifiers/instrument_id.rs:83-118`). Existing ruleset-mode tests bypass this by hand-building fully-qualified `"ACTIVE-RT.POLYMARKET"` strings.
- Current ruleset selection contract is `Activate { instrument_id }` / `Clear` only (`src/platform/runtime.rs:758-771`). No timing metadata, no fee data, no ranked alternatives for strategy EV decisions.
- No cross-market preemption guard. If selector decides to switch while a position is open, the runtime would switch under the position.
- No strategy-side fee seam. Gamma fee fields (`makerBaseFee`, `takerBaseFee`) are explicitly marked unreliable by NT upstream (`nautilus_trader/crates/adapters/polymarket/src/http/parse.rs:111-114`, verbatim: *"Gamma API fee fields are unreliable, actual fees come from the CLOB API at trade time"*). The preserved `#118` branch had been propagating Gamma fees uncritically into `CandidateMarket` — using data NT rejects.
- `event_slugs` data-client filter is exact-match only (`src/validate.rs:1131-1161`, `src/clients/polymarket.rs:61`, NT `adapters/polymarket/src/providers.rs:211`). A 5-minute ETH up/down family rolls a new slug every 5 minutes (`eth-updown-5m-<unix_ts>`); exact-match cannot follow the family.
- Two preserved branches (`issue-118-runtime-enablement@27e7ef47`, `issue-126-polymarket-depth-followup@be61a02f`) were closed without merge and contain a mix of correct seam shapes and review-flagged anti-patterns: synthetic-incumbent `CandidateMarket` with fabricated fields, silent mutex-poison bypass in preemption guard, misnamed "delta-backed fallback" test (proves NT-generic behavior, not Polymarket-specific), unpinned `rust_decimal = "1"`, Gamma fee propagation. Not cherry-pick-able wholesale.

**Why it matters:** Money. Live supervised trading on a real strategy is the gate for every subsequent decision — profitability validation, sizing calibration, ownership-rotation prioritization, multi-market expansion. Until the minimum path is built honestly, every subsequent architectural decision is premature.

## Approach

**Reasoning framework:** First principles, per the 2026-04-12 task-output investigation postmortem (`/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/docs/2026-04-12-task-output-investigation-postmortem.md`). Binary **proven / not proven** only; no "mostly understood" reasoning. Dependency-table completeness required before implementation. Runtime artifacts beat reviews. Every invariant on the critical path verified by a file:line citation on `main@005d489` or a pinned-NT source read at `af2aefc24451ed5c51b94e64459421f1dd540bfb`.

### Epistemic process applied to reach 100% confidence

1. **Epistemic standard locked first.** Read the task-output investigation postmortem to anchor the standard before touching any code. Key rules: no "mostly," binary status only, do not let implementation discover prerequisites, reviews are not substitutes for runtime artifacts.

2. **Parallel research agents dispatched** for independent investigation from isolated contexts:
   - Agent A — postmortem and issue reading: extract claimed blockers vs. proven blockers from #110 / #118 / #126 / #129 / #132 and all their comments.
   - Agent B — branch diffs: categorize every change on `27e7ef47` and `be61a02f` against main as (A) real capability, (B) infra/plumbing, (C) tests/docs, (D) churn/dead-end.
   - Agent C — current-main code trace: verify strategy-kind gates, data flow, exec flow, runtime wiring, NT adapter surface, LiveNode API.

3. **Direct verification** on every non-trivial claim. File:line reads on `main@005d489` for all citations; pinned NT (`af2aefc`) source reads for every adapter / cache / node claim. No reliance on agent summaries for load-bearing facts.

4. **Cross-audit with Codex** running the same investigation in parallel. Compared reports round by round. Substantive disagreements were adjudicated by direct source verification, not argumentation:
   - Codex caught **Gamma-fees-unreliable finding** (NT `http/parse.rs:111-114` comment + `let maker_fee: Option<Decimal> = None`). Claude's original plan had carried Gamma fee fields; corrected after verification.
   - Codex caught **CLOB `/fee-rate` endpoint already exists** in NT (`execution/submitter.rs:81-114`: `get_fee_rate_bps(token_id)` with 5-min TTL + stale-on-failure fallback). This made `PolymarketClobFeeProvider` the correct Issue-1 seam, replacing Claude's earlier `StaticFeeProvider` (static TOML) proposal.
   - Claude caught **`event_slugs` exact-match limitation** (validator + NT adapter both reject prefix patterns). Codex's original report hadn't flagged this.
   - Claude caught **15m / 1h / 1d non-existence on Polymarket** (verified via live Gamma API query: zero events for those slugs). Pinned scope to 5m only.
   - Both converged on: two ordered issues, `#126` and `#132` rejected as immediate prerequisites, `#118` branch not cherry-pickable wholesale.

5. **Red-team review round** (Codex adversarial review of Claude's final plan). Seven findings, all accepted:
   - **HIGH F1:** dual-source market-family definition (ruleset `tag_slug` + `event_slug_matchers`). → Derive data-client matcher from ruleset; one source of truth.
   - **HIGH F2:** "cached-incumbent ledger" is a second source of truth. → Use NT `cache.positions_open(...)` only; gate on `NodeState::Running` for reconciliation-complete signal.
   - **HIGH F3:** ownership/claim boundary across switches not frozen. → Explicit same-session attribution test via `ClientOrderId` + accepted-gap paragraph for restart/manual-order attribution (`#132`).
   - **MED F4:** `StrategyBuilder::build(&Value)` signature underspecified vs. injected `FeeProvider`. → Define `StrategyBuildContext` dependency bundle passed to every builder.
   - **MED F5:** resolution_basis example wrong (`"ETH/USD Chainlink"` vs. canonical `chainlink_ethusd` per `src/platform/resolution_basis.rs:112-123`). → Fix example; no parser change needed.
   - **MED F6:** `FeeProvider` hot-path guarantee missing. → Sync `fee_bps()` + async `warm()` + fail-closed on cold miss (matches NT submitter stale-fallback semantics).
   - **MED F7:** newly-discovered market subscribability not a proof gate. → Added end-to-end integration test: selector chooses new market B → data client refresh loads B → strategy subscribes to B's L2 deltas successfully.

6. **Second red-team pass** (Codex review of Claude's F1–F7 corrections). Three implementation details tightened:
   - F2a — use real NT cache primitive `cache.positions_open(venue, instrument_id, strategy_id, account_id, side)` (`common/src/cache/mod.rs:3213`), not a hypothetical helper.
   - F2b — anchor "reconciliation complete" to `NodeState::Running` (verified: `nautilus_trader/crates/live/src/node.rs:98-105` enum + `:492-599` reconciliation flow + `:707` transition to Running after reconciliation).
   - F6 — keep fee warming inside the strategy, not the runtime. Strategy triggers `fee_provider.warm(token_id)` on snapshot; sets `fees_ready_for_active = false` until cache is warm; fail-closed on cold miss. Platform stays pure.

7. **Plan frozen** after both parties agreed: "stop debating the architecture; freeze and execute."

### Starting points (file:line)

- `src/main.rs:162-173` — strategy-mode match arm (one of five kind gates)
- `src/validate.rs:668, 1256-1458` — validation gates (allowlist, kind-specific config, ruleset-mode exec_tester requirement)
- `src/platform/runtime.rs:340-428` — `wire_platform_runtime` (ruleset-gated)
- `src/platform/runtime.rs:119-122, 758-771` — current `Activate`/`Clear` command envelope
- `src/platform/runtime.rs:626-788` — `runtime_strategy_template`, `reconcile_runtime_strategy`, `build_runtime_exec_tester`
- `src/platform/polymarket_catalog.rs:82-123` — instrument-id catalog bug (`first_token_id`)
- `src/platform/ruleset.rs` — `CandidateMarket`, `SelectionEvaluation`
- `src/strategies/mod.rs:1`, `src/strategies/exec_tester.rs` — strategy module surface
- `src/clients/polymarket.rs:15-25, 61-65` — Polymarket data client config + `EventSlugFilter`
- `src/platform/reference.rs:40`, `src/platform/reference_actor.rs` — already-landed reference fusion layer
- `src/platform/resolution_basis.rs:112-125` — canonical basis format (`chainlink_ethusd`)
- `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/af2aefc/crates/adapters/polymarket/src/http/parse.rs:111-114` — NT declares Gamma fees unreliable
- `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/af2aefc/crates/adapters/polymarket/src/execution/submitter.rs:81-114` — CLOB `/fee-rate` cached fetch
- `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/af2aefc/crates/adapters/polymarket/src/execution/parse.rs:279-285` — commission formula
- `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/af2aefc/crates/common/src/cache/mod.rs:3213` — real cache API for open positions
- `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/af2aefc/crates/live/src/node.rs:98-105, 492-707, 1256-1282` — NodeState, reconciliation flow, `add_strategy`
- `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/nautilus_trader-*/af2aefc/crates/live/src/manager.rs:2213-2240` — external-order attribution path
- `/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/docs/2026-04-12-task-output-investigation-postmortem.md` — epistemic standard

## Expected Outcome

This epic is "done" when both child issues are merged AND live fills are confirmed with a written sign-off to scale size. Not "merged with mocks" alone.

- [ ] Child Issue 1 (runtime enablement) merged — all its acceptance gates pass.
- [ ] Child Issue 2 (ETH 5m Chainlink adaptive taker) merged — all its acceptance gates pass.
- [ ] Supervised paper run on mock-harness `eth-updown-5m-*` market: one full entry/exit cycle with mock fills.
- [ ] Supervised live run at minimum size ($50 initial cap) against one real `eth-updown-5m-*` market: one `Limit`+`FOK` order observed at the Polymarket CLOB; fill or kill observed; any opened position managed through resolution.
- [ ] Post-run verification: fee source trace confirmed (CLOB `/fee-rate` used, not Gamma fields); no unexpected `EXTERNAL`-tagged orders; operator runbook updated with observed fee schedule and any edge cases.

## Risks

- **Strategy engineering budget.** EV math, lead arbitration, robust sizing, and exit calculus are the actual product. Time-to-first-fill is dominated by Issue 2 implementation quality, not infra. → Issue 2 scoped to 5m-only with explicit non-goals; no scope creep.
- **Chainlink feed identifier mismatch.** If operator configures a different feed than the one Polymarket uses for resolution, EV math is systematically wrong. → Verify feed id against a resolved historical 5m market before first live run; runbook gate.
- **CLOB `/fee-rate` eventual consistency.** Strategy-side `PolymarketClobFeeProvider` and NT exec submitter both cache with 5-min TTL independently. Fee charged at fill may differ from fee used in EV by up to one rotation. → Accepted as ≤ ~0.01% EV drift; monitor observed-vs-configured fee delta post-fill.
- **External-order attribution on restart.** Strategy registers with `external_order_claims = None`. Orders open from a prior session matching our account re-attach via `ClientOrderId` reconciliation; any truly external orders (manual operator placement, adapter anomaly) tag as `EXTERNAL` and require manual reconcile. → Accepted as `#132` gap; mitigated by small initial size and supervised operation.
- **Reconciliation timeout.** If `timeout_reconciliation_secs` expires before reconciliation completes, NT transitions to `Running` anyway with a warning log. Selector must not emit switches during the incomplete window. → Generous timeout (≥ 60s); log-watch alarm on reconciliation-timeout warnings; selector defensively emits `Idle` snapshots while `state() != Running`.
- **Msgbus handler `!Send` constraints.** Strategy runs on LocalSet. Cross-task state uses `Rc<RefCell<_>>` or `Arc<Mutex<_>>` with explicit poisoning policy. → Decide per structure in Issue 1 implementation; document in module header; no silent mutex-poison bypass (a specific #118-branch reviewer finding).
- **Blast radius.** Issue 1 refactors `src/platform/runtime.rs`, `src/validate.rs`, and `src/platform/polymarket_catalog.rs` — touches every existing platform test. Issue 2 is additive strategy code. → Both can be reverted with clean merges; Issue 1 behavior is gated (no new strategy kind registered until Issue 2 lands, so Issue 1 alone is a strict plumbing upgrade with no live-behavior change except the instrument-id fix).

## Test Plan

This epic's test plan is the union of both child issues' acceptance gates plus the end-to-end verification sequence. Each child issue owns its own detailed test plan.

High-level verification sequence:

- [ ] Issue 1 CI green (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo deny check`, `cargo test`).
- [ ] Issue 1 integration tests: real-Gamma-fixture instrument-id round-trip through `InstrumentId::from_str` without panic; persistent-lifecycle across `[Active A] → [Active B] → [Idle] → [Active C]` snapshot sequence (identical `component_id`, zero `remove_strategy` calls until shutdown); preemption with mock open position in A suppresses switch to B; slug-prefix matcher expansion against captured Gamma fixture; `PolymarketClobFeeProvider` cache hit + stale-fallback semantics match NT submitter.
- [ ] Issue 1 CI grep assertion: zero read-sites of Gamma `maker_base_fee` / `taker_base_fee` outside the "unreliable" documentation comment.
- [ ] Issue 1 reconciliation-complete gate: selector emits `Idle` while `NodeState != Running`; emits first `Active` snapshot only after transition.
- [ ] Issue 1 newly-discovered market subscribability test (F7): selector chooses B after periodic Gamma refresh → data client has B loaded → strategy subscribes to B's L2 deltas without error within `update_instruments_interval_mins + snapshot_publish_delay`.
- [ ] Issue 2 CI green.
- [ ] Issue 2 integration tests: warmup gating; recovery mode on startup with open position; lead-source fallback on venue failure; uncertainty band widening under jitter; robust EV-maximizing sizing differs from frontier when `risk_lambda > 0`; exit on `exit_ev ≥ hold_ev`; forced-flat triggers (stale Chainlink, thin book, freeze window, metadata mismatch); per-market cooldown; one-position invariant; same-session A→B attribution via `ClientOrderId`.
- [ ] Supervised paper run on `tests/live_node_run.rs`-style harness with real config shape: strategy registers through registry, selector emits snapshots, strategy subscribes, submits mock order, fills.
- [ ] Supervised live run at $50 cap against one current `eth-updown-5m-*` market: order observed at Polymarket CLOB; fee charged at fill matches EV assumption within ~0.01% drift band.

## Architectural Principles

Child issues must honor these to stay systematic (no hardcodes, one source of truth per concept):

1. **Strategy kinds live in a trait + registry.** `trait StrategyBuilder { fn kind(); fn validate_config(&Value, &mut Vec<ValidationError>); fn build(&Value, &StrategyBuildContext) -> Result<BoxedStrategy>; }`. All dispatch sites (validator, main, runtime) consult the registry. Adding a kind is a single registration call. `VALID_STRATEGY_TYPES` derives from `registry.kinds()`.
2. **Selection is data, not commands.** `RuntimeSelectionSnapshot { ruleset_id, decision, eligible_candidates, published_at_ms }` on msgbus topic `platform.runtime.selection.<strategy_id>`. No `Activate`/`Clear` RPCs.
3. **Strategy owns its lifecycle across switches.** Built once at startup, kept alive through all selection changes, removed only on shutdown. Per-interval state (interval-open, warmup counter) resets on switch; cross-switch state (cooldown ledger, recovery flag, component_id) persists.
4. **Preemption is truthful suppression via NT cache.** Sole open-position source: `cache.positions_open(None, None, Some(&strategy_id), None, None)` (`common/src/cache/mod.rs:3213`). Gate on `LiveNodeHandle::state() == NodeState::Running`. No custom ledger. No synthetic `CandidateMarket` with fabricated fields.
5. **One Polymarket instrument-id formatter.** `polymarket_instrument_id(condition_id, token_id) -> InstrumentId` lives in exactly one module. `CandidateMarket` carries `condition_id`, `up_token_id`, `down_token_id` — strategy picks the side.
6. **Fees via `FeeProvider` trait; default impl wraps CLOB `/fee-rate`.** Sync `fee_bps()` (cache-only) for hot path. Async `warm()` triggered by strategy on snapshot. Fail-closed on cold miss. Stale-fallback on refresh failure (matches NT submitter at `execution/submitter.rs:96-113`). Strategy holds `Arc<dyn FeeProvider>`. No Gamma fee fields propagate into `CandidateMarket`.
7. **Market-family filter derived from ruleset.** `derive_event_slug_matchers(&RulesetConfig) -> Vec<SlugMatcher>` is the single function that expresses which markets the data client follows. Operator writes the ruleset once; data client follows.
8. **Reference pipeline stays ruleset-gated.** No unbundling in this epic. Rotation requires ruleset mode; reference already requires rulesets.
9. **Kind-specific config validation dispatches via registry.** Shared fields (`strategy_id`, `client_id`, etc.) validated once. Kind-specific fields validated by the registered builder's `validate_config`.
10. **Order-type policy (FOK, post-only, etc.) lives in strategy builders, not in the platform validator.** This was `#126`'s closure reason; do not repeat.

## Already Landed (Do Not Rebuild)

On `main@005d489`:
- Per-venue reference observation fields (`src/platform/reference.rs:40`, tested at `tests/reference_actor.rs:239`)
- Multi-venue fusion with `base_weight` / `stale_after_ms` / `disable_after_ms` (`src/platform/reference_actor.rs` + runtime registration at `src/platform/runtime.rs:430-463`)
- Generic ETH/Chainlink basis parsing with canonical form `chainlink_ethusd` (`src/platform/resolution_basis.rs:112-125`, tested `tests/polymarket_catalog.rs:208`)
- Chainlink ETH/USD WS data client (`src/clients/chainlink.rs`)
- SSM secret resolution (`src/secrets.rs`)
- Normalized sink / audit spool (`src/normalized_sink.rs`, `src/platform/audit.rs`)
- Truthful depth contract: `order_book_depths = unsupported` (`contracts/polymarket.toml:20`)

In pinned NT (`af2aefc`):
- Polymarket L2 book deltas (`BookType::L2_MBP`) at `adapters/polymarket/src/data.rs:1061`
- Polymarket `Limit` + `TimeInForce::Fok` submission at `adapters/polymarket/src/execution/mod.rs:730-801`
- CLOB `/fee-rate` endpoint + 5-min TTL cache + stale-fallback at `adapters/polymarket/src/execution/submitter.rs:81-114`
- Commission formula `size * (fee_bps/10000) * price * (1-price)` at `adapters/polymarket/src/execution/parse.rs:279-285`
- Cache open-position primitive `positions_open(venue, instrument_id, strategy_id, account_id, side)` at `common/src/cache/mod.rs:3213`
- NodeState enum with `Running = reconciliation-complete` semantics at `live/src/node.rs:98-105, 492-707`

## Live Target Verified (as of 2026-04-12)

- Polymarket family: `eth-updown-5m-*` (new market every 5 minutes)
- Chainlink ETH/USD settled via `https://data.chain.link/streams/eth-usd`
- Sample live market: `eth-updown-5m-1775982300`, end `2026-04-12T08:30:00Z`, liquidity ~$9,650, order min $5, `acceptingOrders: true`, `enableOrderBook: true`
- Binary outcomes: `["Up", "Down"]` (decided by Chainlink close price >= open price over the 5-min window)
- `eth-updown-15m`, `eth-updown-1h`, `eth-updown-1d` variants **do not exist** on Polymarket (verified via Gamma API query)

## Rejected Paths

Recorded so future sessions do not re-explore:

- **Continuing the #130 Phase 3 chain (`#118` → `#126` → `#129` → `#110` → `#132`) wholesale.** `#118`'s preserved PR `#128` was closed with review findings that were never resolved (synthetic incumbent, silent mutex-poison bypass, misnamed "delta-backed fallback" test, unpinned `rust_decimal`, Gamma fee propagation). `#126`'s preserved PR `#131` was closed for user architectural objection to policy encoding in `validate.rs`, not a technical dead-end. `#129` and `#132` are triggered only by behaviors that don't exist yet. Chain was overstaged for the minimum rotating run.
- **Strategy-mode with one static market and no rulesets.** 5m markets live ~5 minutes at resolution, so a truly static operator-pinned market requires restarting bolt every 5 minutes OR reproducing rotation inside the strategy badly. Reference pipeline is already ruleset-gated; unbundling is more work than using ruleset mode.
- **Widening scope to "ETH any" or "ETH 5m + 15m".** 15m / 1h / 1d variants do not exist on Polymarket. ETH price-level markets (`what-price-will-ethereum-hit-before-2027`) resolve via aggregators at year-end, not Chainlink streams, and require a different EV model — turns one strategy into a framework.
- **Cherry-picking from preserved branches wholesale.** Reuse type *names and shapes* from `#118` branch (`RuntimeSelectionSnapshot`, `eligible_candidates`, `runtime_selection_topic`) but rewrite implementations fresh with review feedback applied. Do NOT copy: synthetic incumbent with fabricated fields, silent mutex-poison bypass, misnamed test, unpinned `rust_decimal`, Gamma fee propagation.
- **Unbundling Chainlink reference from ruleset mode.** Minimum rotating path uses ruleset mode, which already requires reference. Unbundling is unnecessary work.
- **Native `OrderBookDepth10` support for Polymarket.** `contracts/polymarket.toml:20` truthfully declares unsupported; NT L2 book deltas are sufficient for taker EV math on a binary market.
- **Dynamic `external_order_claims` rotation on market switch.** Accepted as `#132` gap for this epic. Same-session attribution via `ClientOrderId` is proven safe; restart and external-order attribution are operator-reconciled.

## Accepted Gaps

Documented here so they are not rediscovered as bugs:

- **`external_order_claims` is static within a session.** `LiveNode::add_strategy` (`live/src/node.rs:1266-1272`) registers claims ONCE at add time via `exec_manager.claim_external_orders(...)`. No public dynamic-update API. Initial strategy registers with `external_order_claims: None`. Consequence: external (non-strategy-submitted) orders take NT's `EXTERNAL` fallback path (`live/src/manager.rs:2213-2240`) and require operator reconciliation. Same-session orders we submit ourselves are attributed via `ClientOrderId` regardless of claims — verified safe. Dynamic claim rotation is `#132` territory.
- **CLOB fee-rate TTL drift.** Up to one 5-min rotation of drift between strategy-side fee cache and exec-side fee cache. Accepted as ≤ ~0.01% EV drift per trade.
- **No `modify_order` on Polymarket.** NT exec client rejects modify (`adapters/polymarket/src/execution/mod.rs:787-801`). Strategy must cancel+replace if exit price changes.
- **Single active ruleset restriction.** `src/validate.rs:1386-1396` enforces one ruleset. Fine for 5m-only. Concurrent 5m + other-family would require lifting this later.

## Confidence

100% on engineering shape. Every claim in this epic maps to a file:line artifact on `main@005d489` or pinned NT `af2aefc`. Audit rounds:

1. Claude primary investigation → 100% claim
2. Codex parallel investigation → 100% claim, plus Gamma-fees + CLOB-fee-seam corrections
3. Claude re-verification of Codex corrections → verified, plan updated
4. Codex red-team review → 7 findings (3 HIGH, 4 MED), all accepted
5. Claude corrections emitted → plan updated
6. Codex second red-team → 3 implementation tightenings (real cache API, `NodeState::Running`, fee-warm inside strategy), all accepted
7. Both parties: "stop debating, freeze"

No "mostly understood" reasoning is used anywhere. Profitability of `#110`'s strategy is **not** assessed in this epic — that is an assumption per user directive. Fee discipline, data discipline, and lifecycle discipline are the engineering invariants this epic owns.

## Relations

Related to:
- `#110` — original strategy issue; scope inherited and reshaped (5m-only, operator-pinned instrument via ruleset selection).
- `#118` — rejected as wholesale prerequisite; `RuntimeSelectionSnapshot` / `eligible_candidates` names reused, implementations rewritten fresh.
- `#126` — rejected as prerequisite; native depth10 not needed; policy-in-validator approach explicitly not repeated.
- `#129` — rejected as immediate prerequisite; persistent-lifecycle folded into child Issue 1.
- `#130` — prior Phase 3 epic; this epic **supersedes its decomposition** (does not sub-ordinate under it).
- `#132` — deferred; accepted platform gap (external-order-claim rotation).
- `#128` — closed PR for `#118`; reference only, not cherry-pickable wholesale.
- `#131` — closed PR for `#126`; reference only, not cherry-pickable wholesale.
- `#37` — landed dependency (Chainlink ingest + snapshot contract).
- `#109` — landed dependency (generic resolution-basis parsing).
- `#121` — Chainlink transport hardening; adjacent, not blocking.
- `#127` — not in scope for this epic.

Depends on: None. `main@005d489` is the starting point.

Blocks: Child Issue 1 (runtime enablement) and Child Issue 2 (ETH 5m Chainlink adaptive taker) — created after this epic.

Spawned from: Emergency investigation triggered 2026-04-12 after closure of `#128` and `#131`.

issue.title: normalized_sink inline capture path — evaluate sidecar extraction
issue.body:
## Problem

The capture pipeline (`normalized_sink.rs`) runs inline in the live trading binary. It is wired at `src/main.rs:144-154` and subscribes to the in-process NT msgbus. Capture failure can trigger live-node stop. While capture today is already gated (empty `streaming.catalog_path` disables it), extraction to a separate process would fully isolate capture failures from trading correctness.

This issue is **deferred** — tracked for visibility, not scheduled for execution until a trigger fires.

## Root Problem Analysis

**Current behavior (confirmed by D3 arbitration across Gemini + MiniMax + GLM):**
- `src/normalized_sink.rs:549` — `wire_normalized_sinks` creates a `FeatherWriter` + JSONL sidecars and spawns a local task subscribed to `data.quotes.*.*`, `events.order.*`, etc.
- `src/main.rs:144-154` — wiring happens only if `cfg.streaming.catalog_path.trim().is_empty()` is false.
- `src/main.rs:162-170` — sink failure receiver is `tokio::select!`'d alongside `node.run()`. A sink failure triggers node stop.
- Zero references to `normalized_sink` in `src/platform/runtime.rs`.

The sink is:
- **Not** on the strategy-input path.
- **Not** on the order-delivery path.
- **Is** a passive msgbus observer writing to disk.
- **Can** kill the live node on write error.

**Structural risk:** a disk-full error, a capture bug, or any unexpected I/O error in the sink can trigger a live-node stop.

**Mitigation today:** larger EC2 instance pushes the disk-pressure risk window out significantly.

**Arbitration findings (all three arbiters):** the sink is an independent capture pipeline. Moving it to a sidecar is architecturally safe — live trading can run with `catalog_path = ""`. Extraction is feasible but non-trivial (the in-process msgbus is process-local; a sidecar would read the already-written Feather/JSONL files, similar to how `lake_batch` already operates).

## Specific Evidence

- D3 arbitration verbatim (Gemini + MiniMax + GLM) — all three confirmed the sink is independent, passive, and safely disableable. Full transcripts in epic #137 comment 7c.

## Reproducible Procedures

```bash
# From repo root on main@005d489:

# 1. Sink wiring:
rg -n 'wire_normalized_sinks|normalized_sink' src/main.rs src/platform/

# 2. Sink failure path:
rg -n 'stop_handle|stop\(\)' src/normalized_sink.rs

# 3. Confirm empty catalog_path disables the sink:
rg -n 'catalog_path.*is_empty|catalog_path.*trim' src/main.rs
```

## Symptoms

- Sink failure can kill live trading.
- Any future capture logic grows inside the live binary.

## Context

bolt-v2 originally ran capture inline (NT's built-in FeatherWriter pattern). bolt-v1 intended external capture; that was not carried forward into bolt-v2. User's stated preference (session on 2026-04-12): sidecar is the correct design, but not urgent because the inline risk window is long on a larger EC2.

## Priority Tier

**Deferred**. Priority **P4**. Execution triggers:
- **Trigger 1:** first capture-induced live-trading outage.
- **Trigger 2:** before scaling to more markets / venues (more data volume = more sink write pressure).

Do not schedule this issue for execution until one of the above fires.

Tier criterion: "Trigger-based; execution requires a specified event."

## Scope Boundaries

**In scope:** the decision to extract; the extraction surface.

**Out of scope:** NT's msgbus behavior. Live-trading logic. `lake_batch` semantics. **Actual sidecar design — drafted when a trigger fires, not now.**

## Blocks / Depends On

**Depends on:** Epic #137 (for methodology pointer); no execution blocker beyond the trigger events.

**Blocks:** nothing.

## Relations

Part of epic #137 as deferred follow-up. Empirical evidence: D3 arbitration (Gemini + MiniMax + GLM), verbatim in epic comment 7c.

issue.title: infra(ci): add EIP preflight check to deploy job
issue.body:
## Problem Statement

The `bolt-polymarket` Elastic IP (EIP `eipalloc-0bfd66b94102077e0`, address `34.248.143.2`) was associated with bolt-v2-polymarket (`i-08dee6aefe9a5b02c`) on 2026-04-13 (see #152). The stable source IP is load-bearing for Polymarket's auth flow — a different source IP triggers a signing loop on CLOB authentication, which breaks live trading.

Today, nothing prevents that EIP from silently drifting off the instance. Possible drift scenarios:

- Manual detach/release in the AWS console
- Replacing the instance without re-associating
- Someone assuming the EIP is "just informational" and releasing it

If drift happens, the first symptom is the Polymarket signing loop — visible but disruptive.

**Why it matters:** one CI step can block deploys onto an instance where the EIP has drifted, preventing us from shipping new code onto a misconfigured box.

## Approach

Add a preflight step in the `deploy` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs after the S3 upload and before marking the deploy successful. The step should:

1. Query AWS by **tag**, not hardcoded IDs, matching rule #1 (NO HARDCODES):
   - EIP: `describe-addresses --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=bolt-polymarket`
   - Instance: `describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=bolt-v2-polymarket`
2. Verify the EIP's `InstanceId` equals the looked-up instance ID.
3. Fail the job with a clear message on mismatch, success otherwise.

A reusable shell script at `scripts/preflight-eip.sh` keeps the logic out of the workflow YAML and lets operators run the same check locally before a manual SSM restart.

**IAM change required:** The deploy role referenced by `vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` currently has (at most) S3 write. To run the preflight it also needs:
- `ec2:DescribeAddresses`
- `ec2:DescribeInstances`

Both are read-only, no data risk.

## Expected Outcome

- `scripts/preflight-eip.sh` committed, executable, uses tag-based lookup, exits non-zero on drift with a human-readable message.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` deploy job runs the script after S3 upload.
- Deploy role's attached IAM policy has the two new `ec2:Describe*` permissions.
- A deliberate test (e.g., temporarily detaching the EIP in a non-prod clone, or stubbing the expected instance tag) shows CI failing with the drift message.

## Alternatives Considered

**Option 2: systemd `ExecStartPre=` on the instance** — run the same check before `bolt-v2` starts. Rejected for now because:
- `bolt-v2` only restarts on deploy, so it triggers about as often as the CI check would.
- Adds server-side moving parts: AWS CLI on the instance, IAM perm on `bolt-polymarket-exec-role`, unit file change.
- Drift happening *during* a running session wouldn't restart the service on its own — it would still surface via the Polymarket signing loop, same as today.

**Option 3: manual `just preflight-eip` recipe** — weakest; has to be remembered. Not chosen as the primary mechanism, but the committed shell script enables this as a side benefit.

**Doing nothing** — defensible. The signing loop is its own early warning, and drift is rare under a single-operator regime. Option 1 is worth doing specifically because it converts "we'll notice when it breaks in prod" into "we block a deploy onto a broken box," which is a real asymmetric improvement. Not worth more than a P3 until evidence of recurring drift.

## Risks

- **Low.** Read-only AWS call, no state mutation. Worst case: a CI bug causes false failure, blocking a deploy until fixed.
- **IAM policy change is reversible** — detach the added permissions.
- **If the EIP is legitimately reassigned** (e.g., swapping to a new bolt-v2 instance during disaster recovery), the preflight would fail loudly; that's correct behavior — force the operator to re-associate intentionally.

## Test Plan

1. Run `scripts/preflight-eip.sh` locally with correct AWS creds → prints `OK: EIP ... correctly attached to ...`, exits 0.
2. In a sandbox (or by temporarily overriding `INSTANCE_NAME` to a non-existent tag), run the script → exits non-zero with the drift message.
3. Push a dummy tag (`v0.0.0-test`) to trigger the deploy job → verify the preflight step runs after S3 upload and passes.
4. Simulate drift (temporarily disassociate the EIP in a dev account, not prod) → verify the next CI deploy job fails at the preflight step with the expected message.

## Relations
- Tracked by epic #169.

Related to #152 (recorded the EIP association on 2026-04-13 and documented that Polymarket's signing flow depends on a stable source IP).

issue.body:
## Problem
Additional tools may help catch AI-generated tech debt, but too many gates can create noise, overlap, and process debt.

## Goal
Evaluate broader guardrails after the deterministic verifier MVP exists.

## Candidates
- ast-grep expansion
- Semgrep
- SonarCloud/SonarQube tuning
- CodeQL custom queries
- OPA/Conftest
- reviewdog/Danger
- additional AI reviewer workflows

## Acceptance Criteria
For each candidate, document:
- Failure classes it catches beyond Issue 1.
- Whether it is deterministic enough to block merges.
- Expected false-positive risk.
- Required workflow/check impact.
- Whether it fits existing source-fence/verifier patterns.
- Recommendation: adopt, pilot advisory, defer, or reject.

## Out Of Scope
- Adding a new blocking tool without a concrete missed failure class.
- Making AI reviewers authoritative.
- Duplicating existing source-fence verifier coverage.

issue.title: Add bulk merge-queue mode for planned multi-PR batches
issue.body:
## Problem

Mergify's speculative queue PR title/body only represents the active check batch, not the full waiting queue. During planned multi-PR merge sessions this is confusing: operators may queue several approved PRs, but the visible queue PR can show only a subset such as `#1094 + #1093` while other accepted PRs remain in "Preparing checks".

The immediate cause is the current `default` queue rule:

- `batch_size.min: 2`
- `batch_size.max: 10`
- `batch_max_wait_time: 5 minutes`
- `merge_queue.max_parallel_checks: 1`

`max: 10` is only a ceiling, not a target. With `min: 2`, Mergify may start checking the first eligible pair before the operator finishes queueing the full intended group. Because only one speculative check can run at a time, later accepted PRs are placed behind that first active batch and get a separate proof PR.

Observed example:

- Intended operator batch: `#1094 #1093 #1064 #1060 #1059 #1052`
- Actual first proof PR: `#1100` for `#1094 + #1093`
- Actual second proof PR: `#1101` for `#1064 + #1052 + #1060 + #1059`

The current behavior is reasonable for normal low-latency merging, but it is not explicit enough for planned "merge these N PRs together" sessions.

## Expected Outcome

Provide a clear long-term path for intentional bulk merge sessions so the active Mergify proof PR title/body names the full intended batch when possible, while preserving the existing default queue behavior for ordinary merges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add an explicit bulk merge mode separate from the existing `default` queue.
- Bulk mode must require an intentional operator signal, such as a `bulk-merge` label or another clearly documented queue-selection convention.
- Bulk mode must not start a proof batch merely because two PRs are ready when the operator intended a larger batch.
- Bulk mode must preserve or strengthen the existing required conditions:
  - `approved-reviews-by = sp-reviewer`
  - `check-success = gate`
  - `check-success = backtester-gate`
  - `check-success = actionlint`
  - `check-success = host-health`
  - no closed/draft/conflicting PRs
  - no unresolved review threads
  - last-push approval remains enforced by branch rules
- The existing `default` queue must remain optimized for ordinary low-latency merges and must not be retuned into a high-latency bulk-only path.
- The operator workflow must document how to queue a planned bulk batch, including the expected timing/order for applying the signal and posting `@Mergifyio queue` commands.
- The implementation must avoid repo-owned rewriting of Mergify draft PR title/body unless there is no safer option; Mergify may overwrite metadata, and PR metadata edits can trigger extra workflows.

## Approach Notes

Recommended direction:

- Add a separate Mergify queue rule for planned bulk sessions, for example triggered by a `bulk-merge` label.
- Configure the bulk rule with an explicit higher minimum batch size or fixed batch size appropriate for planned sessions.
- Preserve `max_parallel_checks: 1` unless there is separate evidence that parallel proof PRs are cost-safe and operationally clear.
- Keep `branch_protection_injection_mode: merge`, queue proof PR behavior, and existing required gates.
- Add verifier coverage so future changes cannot silently relax bulk queue protections.

Potential shape, subject to exact Mergify syntax and live validation:

```yaml
queue_rules:
  - name: bulk
    queue_conditions:
      - label = bulk-merge
    merge_conditions:
      - approved-reviews-by = sp-reviewer
      - check-success = gate
      - check-success = backtester-gate
      - check-success = actionlint
      - check-success = host-health
    branch_protection_injection_mode: merge
    batch_size:
      min: 6
      max: 10
    batch_max_wait_time: 5 minutes
    batch_max_failure_resolution_attempts: 0
    checks_timeout: 150 minutes
    draft_bot_account: null
    merge_method: squash
```

The exact `min` should be chosen deliberately. If the operator needs variable-size batches, document the supported sizes or use labels/rules that make the intended size explicit.

## Risks

- Larger batches increase failure blast radius: one failing PR can block the whole batch.
- Longer wait windows can slow planned merges if the intended group is not fully queued.
- Label-driven queue routing must not bypass approval, review-thread, conflict, or gate requirements.
- A fixed `min: 6` rule is unsuitable for intentional 3- or 4-PR bulk sessions unless additional rules or a documented fallback exist.
- Editing Mergify-created proof PR metadata can create workflow noise and should remain a non-goal unless proven necessary.

## Verification

Static verifier coverage for `.mergify.yml` should enforce:

- `default` queue behavior remains unchanged or intentionally reviewed.
- bulk queue keeps the required review and CI gates.
- bulk queue does not relax conflict/draft/closed protections.
- bulk queue uses queue proof PR behavior rather than in-place checks.
- bulk queue cannot silently become equivalent to the current `min: 2` default path.

Live validation should queue a small approved batch under the bulk rule and confirm:

- Mergify creates a proof PR.
- proof PR title/body names the intended batch.
- `gate` and `backtester-gate` run on the proof PR.
- successful batch merges normally.
- failed batch behavior is understandable and does not dequeue unrelated default/hotfix work unexpectedly.

## Non-Goals

- Do not remove or slow down the existing default queue for ordinary merges.
- Do not weaken branch rules, approval requirements, or CI gates.
- Do not depend on manually editing Mergify proof PR title/body as the primary solution.
- Do not enable parallel speculative checks without separate cost and operator-readability evidence.

## Relations

Related to merge-queue operator workflow observed during PRs #1094, #1093, #1064, #1060, #1059, and #1052.

issue.title: CI: cache system rebuilds existing artifacts — keys hash ci.yml, branch scope isolation defeats reuse, over-quota store drops saves
issue.body:
## Problem
Full CI proofs rebuild artifacts that already exist. Three defects, each verified directly on run 28571284639 (2026-07-02, branch `fix/1162-mq-storm-concurrency`, a Rust-unchanged diff):

1. **Over-inclusive cache keys.** Every `managed-target-v1-*` cache key hashes `'.github/workflows/ci.yml'`, `'justfile'`, and governance scripts (see the `hashFiles(...)` lists in ci.yml — `archive_build_target_cache_key` in the test-archive job and the `build` job's `actions/cache` key). Any CI-governance edit — the dominant recent PR shape — invalidates every build cache. Observed: the run computed novel key hashes matching nothing in the store.
2. **Branch scope isolation defeats reuse.** The run's `nextest-archive-v3-…-836ed0657…` key (Rust-only digest, correctly equal to main's) existed on `refs/heads/main` with identical cache `version` (`05bdb8bb…`, confirmed via `GET /actions/caches?key=…`), yet restore logged `Cache not found`. Historically PR #1157 and main each built and saved byte-identical archives 83 minutes apart. Result: ~10GB of the 12.65GB store is the same ~2.2GB artifact set duplicated across 5 refs.
3. **Over-quota store drops new saves.** The store sits at 12.65GB against GitHub's 10GB cap. The run logged `Cache saved successfully` ×4 (~3.3GB, 07:06–07:11 UTC); by ~08:00 the cache API showed none of them — inventory unchanged at 17 caches / 12.65GB. Saving is currently near-pointless.

Consequence: `build` ran 14 min on a stale prefix-fallback cache and `nextest archive` cold-compiled 18 min while a byte-identical archive sat on main. Cold-vs-warm is ~90% of the historical 14→43 min proof swing.

## Expected Outcome
- A proof whose Rust-relevant inputs (existing nextest tree digest, `ci/nextest-fingerprint.toml` tracked_inputs) are unchanged vs an existing artifact restores that artifact instead of compiling, regardless of which branch built it.
- One stored copy per digest (content-addressed), not one per ref.
- CI-governance edits (ci.yml, justfile, scripts) do not invalidate build/test artifacts whose Rust inputs are unchanged.
- Cache/storage outage or miss degrades to a normal build — never a wrong result, never a red lane (fail-open to build, fail-closed on integrity).
- The `ci-storage-tripwire` guardrail actually fires (scheduled for 24+ days with zero recorded runs — fix or replace as part of this work).

## Approach Notes (decided direction — Option A of the reviewed plan)
- Move `nextest-archive` + `root-bin-sidecars` (and evaluate `managed-target`) to content-addressed S3 keyed by the existing Rust-only nextest digest, reusing the live sccache bucket/auth path (`bolt-v2-ci-cache-*-us-east-2`, already in production on the archive job). Extends #1011's direction.
- Align remaining GH-cache keys to the same Rust-only digest — remove `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `justfile`, and non-Rust scripts from `hashFiles(...)` lists.
- GH Actions cache retains only small, cheap items (cargo registry, tooling).
- Week-one metrics required: S3 egress bytes/run and restore time, with a documented kill-switch back to GH cache.
- Integrity invariant: never restore an artifact whose digest differs from the tested SHA's Rust inputs. Reuse-eligibility policy (event types, provenance) is tracked separately in the archive-reuse issue; this issue is storage/keying only.

## Risks
- Wrong-artifact reuse — mitigated by the digest gate (unchanged semantics, same digest already used today).
- S3 egress cost — measured in week one; kill-switch documented.
- Reversible: config/workflow + script changes; revert restores current behavior.

## Verification
- Re-run a CI-governance-only diff post-fix: archive/build restore instead of compile; proof wall-clock recorded before/after.
- Fixture/unit coverage for digest keying and fail-open paths per repo testing rules.
- One week of egress + hit-rate metrics attached before closing.

## Relations
Related to #1011
Related to #939
Related to #950
Related to #951
Related to #929
Related to #333
Related to #1162

issue.title: Track runner identity in nextest reuse provenance
issue.body:
## Problem
Nextest archive reuse currently binds git-tracked workflow/provenance inputs, but it does not record the resolved GitHub runner identity behind `vars.CI_RUNNER_*`.

If a repo variable such as `CI_RUNNER_MANAGED_HEAVY` is changed outside git, consumers may reuse a source archive produced on the previous runner label for the configured lookback window.

## Expected Outcome
Nextest reuse must fail closed when the source run's runner identity differs from the current run's resolved runner identity.

## Approach Notes
- Record resolved runner identity/tier in nextest fingerprint or CI provenance.
- Compare source vs current runner identity before allowing reuse.
- Avoid comparing only the literal `${{ vars.CI_RUNNER_* }}` expression.
- Keep PR #1182 scoped; this is follow-up hardening.

## Risks
Moderate CI plumbing risk. The important part is comparing runtime-resolved runner identity, not git-tracked config text alone.

## Verification
- Unit test: matching runner identity allows reuse.
- Unit test: changed runner identity rejects reuse.
- Verifier/docs updated if new workflow arguments or provenance fields are added.
- Exact-head CI evidence.
